column3: Lenovo Vibe K5 Plus (Dark Grey, 16 GB)
column6: After couple of weeks of use, I do like it.
column7:
I am like many, hobbyist smart phone user, but like many, due to my purchase power, tends to buy entry or mid range phones, so my review will be comparing the phone with likes of MI, Moto, and similar priced / configuration Samsung phones.
  

  **Flipkart Offer / Service and over all EXP**
  

  On offer days, such as BBD, bank tie up (extra bank/cc discount) and delivery speed seemed much better than others, very satisfied with the price and service.
  

  **Design / Looks / Feel**
  

  Design is very slick and nice, looks good and is a head turner at this price range. Though feels little flimsy compare to Moto E/G series but personal choice those are. If you like slick, slim design, you won't be disappointed, specially the back, looks like iPhone.
  

  Mind you, no water resistance and does feel a little delicate darling.
  

  **Camera**
  

  Rear camera though rated 13MP, but will disappoint (compare to Moto G/L640) you with indoor performance (shakes, stabilisation issues) and weaker flash, but if you know to play with Camera settings and get those amazing free apps from store to adjust hardware and your shooting style, you can produce some excellent pictures.
  

  Outdoor photography is satisfactory.
  

  Selfie is kind of ok, at this price, cant ask more.
  

  **Display and touch**
  

  Samsung (likes of ON8) wins hands down, no doubt, but this one isn't bad at all, watching those HD movies in VLC, and I have no complain..
  

  Full HD 441 PPI with proper HD content does blow your mind with full brightness!!
  

  Excellent !!
  

  Big let down is the absence of gorilla glass protection, though the phone ships with a screen guard (make sure some training professional installs the screen guard else you will mess it up).
  

  Touch is smooth and feels satisfactory as soon as you remove the protective display plastic and use it with screen guard or without any.
  

  **Performance**
  

  SD 616 / AD 405 / 3GB RAM, this is basically pretty high end configuration packed into this entry lvl phone. And it shows with gaming, I am heavy COC player, who does occupationally loads up FPS and such, and excellent lag free performance, if you can keep it cool. Mind you, any high end phone with such high power processor will have heating issue for sure.
  

  Specification is top notch, so is performance, avoid prolong gaming under hot sun or outdoor weather.
  

  Multi tasking is a charm with my email/office productivity apps/jobs.
  

  16GB built in with dedicated micro SD slot is more than enough for next year or two.
  

  **Network**
  

  Acceptable call quality, or LTE (Tested AirTel and Jio) data performance, so is with Wifi, no complain at all. Running Dual SIM with LTE DATA does effect battery life, do note, but same I found with any other handset, like Moto G3 or Samsung ON8 or Lumia 640.
  

  GPS is also satisfactory, navigation pointers are accurate enough so is the FM radio, a big plus point since many phones are removing this feature !!
  

  **Sound**
  

  Trust me, you will find your friends turning their heads with this dual speaker Dolby sound. Don't mistake it with a Bluetooth portable speaker but for a phone, certainly its loud but clear enough.
  

  **Battery / Charging **
  

  Yes, like those many negative, when I first booted the device, the settings did report 4 hr battery remailing with 85%, but with the first software update and full night charge before first use, things are much better. With heavy usage (Email/Office apps, lot of COC and little FPS games with whatsapp, and around 90 mins of talking) on an average, by day end, 6:30 PM, I am still with close to 50% battery.
  

  Charger with 1.5 Ah is a downer, is though it charges the phone super quick, but cant use any other charger or powerbank (unless it has 1.5 Ah or higher) for this phone.
  

  Phone does heat up while charging, so avoid heavy gaming.
  


  **Software**
  

  Clean android given, not much bloatware, some apps are pre-installed but you can remove them from app settings.
  

  I hate the Vibe UI, nothing to do with any performance issue, but just personal taste.
  

  But happy to see junk free stock ROM. Its 5.1 but expecting a 6.0 update soon.
  

  **Price**
  

  Very good display and high end specs at this price is something to consider !!
  

  My vote, you can Buy it..

Have been using it for the past 1 month. No issues absolutely. Firstly thanks to Flipkart for very good packaging of the product and quick delivery :) Its actually best customer service that I personally rely completely on Flipkart. Thanks to the whole team.
  
  Coming back to the phone :
  
  Pros ~
  
  >Firstly, its a one piece of a kind. Once you take the phone you would realise that. Amazing built quality with aluminium back case and minimum thickness which fits perfectly in your palms.
  
  > Amazing display (full HD 5" , 440 ppi) with absolutely no pixellation even nearest to your observations guaranteed.
  
  >Smooth interface with very minimum customization and boatwares (however there are options to uninstall the preinstalled apps )
  
  >Excellent gaming experience with absolutely no lag . Though expectations were much of a confusing for a sub 10k to run smoothly high-end graphic games, but to my utmost surprise the phone performed excellent . Cheers to 616 snapdragon 64bit chipset with adreno 505 gpu and 3gb ram.
  
  >Camera is no doubt excellent in day light conditions and was average in low light. HDR performance is just wonderful in day time . Worth of using while taking daytime pictures.  With minimum shutter lag and good video recording capabilities , also 5p lens , this 13mp camera just turns around eyes of the observer and hence worth appreciating.
  
  >Front camera (5mp) performance was more than average as expected , however daytime images turned out to be quite great with high detailings.
  
  >With large number of apps installed , still the phone managed to extend its limitations without compromising on the performance. Thanks to the processor ofcourse and 3gb ddr3 ram.
  
  >Lastly the battery, however , is much below average as per as the capacity is concerned , but to my surprise its still a headturner , giving juice to the phone lasting for a day with complete usage (gaming,music,mobile data,wifi,bluetooth). So i was quite satisfied with the battery and no issues.
  
  >The grey colour of the phone is really superb to look at . Satisfied with everything and every details about the phone.
  

  Cons~
  
  >The only problem I found till now is that on using the phone in daylight for a very short time also the phone has heating issues , maybe its because of the aluminium back case.
  

  For those looking for a phone below 10k , guys close your eyes and just blindly rely on Lenovo brand and go ahead to buy this phone . I guarantee you would never the opportunity to regret . :)

column3: Lenovo Vibe K5 Plus (Dark Grey, 16 GB)
column6: Only thing good is 3 gb RAM
column7:
I'm writing this review after using for a week. First of all Flipkart delivery is good as usual.
  
  Now about the phone. I've been using Lenovo A6000 for more than 1.5 years and though that is a basic phone but I really liked its dolby music and camera clarity. So when I purchased this one I really had high hopes but I'd say I'm somewhat disappointed.
  

  BATTERY backup is probably the worst thing in this phone. With 3G on it hardly lasts more than 6 hrs with very little music, little calling, little browsing and absolutely no gaming or anything heavy. This phone needs to be charged twice even for a casual user.
  

  CAMERA is not at all as a 13 mp like in other phones. It's a bit shaky I'll say. Though I yet have to try any 3rd party camera app.
  
  Though the flash is really powerful. Front camera is good but back camera is just OK.
  

  DOLBY SOUND is the main reason I opted for it and yes it's really mesmerizing in headphone.
  
  BUT, in loud places like in a bus or train music is not that loud both in speaker and headphone.
  
  Also I can't alter the equalizer setting manually in DOLBY App even if I selected the Custom mode.
  
  Here also I'm dissatisfied.
  

  INTERNAL MEMORY is only 16 GB which is not a big deal as other phones in this range offer the same.
  
  Good thing is that it doesn't have a Hybrid SIM slot.
  

  To me the only mentionable thing about this phone is 3GB RAM. That is the only good thing about this phone.
  
  Though RAM management is not good, still 3GB (1.8 GB free) is virtually enough for anyone or anything.
  

  So overall being a Lenove user I'm not that satisfied with the product. I chose it mainly for the DOLBY ATMOS but that also I can't configure to get optimum output.
  

  If someone gets tempted by the DOLBY feature and 3GB RAM spec, it's still a good buy,
  
  but otherwise for heavy usage  I think Motorola E3 P is a lot better choice in this range.
  
  Honestly speaking the Battery ruined it all. Do buy an additional power bank with it.

column3: Lenovo Vibe K5 Plus (Dark Grey, 16 GB)
column6: Excellent Screen, awesome sound. Value for Money.
column7:
Got an excellent deal on Big Billion days. Saved 2500 INR !
  

  First things first. The black colored phone shown in pictures is way different that what it is in reality. Think of it as dark grey rather than light black and you will be good.
  

  Looks and fit-and-finish: For a 6700 INR phone, it looks very good.The fit and finish is excellent for the asking price and there are no rough edges or signs of poor assembly . The microphone and speaker holes are perfectly drilled. USB and 3.5 mm jack are placed above so people using it in cars might face some difficulties when placing it in portrait mode. Its considerably lighter than Xiaomi Redmi 3S prime. The rear cover might be prone to scratches and dings because of it metallic nature.
  

  Buttons: Three buttons on the right side are good but don't have a great feedback, say like the iPhone. But they do get the job done.
  
  No physical buttons at front but it has three dedicated navigation touch buttons which are NOT back lit but have haptic feedback. Can be an issue when using phone in dark environments but once you get to know its placement, its not a showstopper.
  

  Screen: 5 inch display with 401 ppi produces sharp images. Color reproduction is excellent. There can be an issue with extremely wide viewing but it is not much of a deal. Youtube viewing in HD is indeed a treat.  Text reading is sharp and it has option to change hue and contrast to have softer tones while reading.
  
  Do note that it DOES NOT HAVE GORILLA GLASS PROTECTION. So you will have to be a little careful. Also there is a little bit of flex when you press the screen with your thumb.
  

  Speakers: They come with Dolby ATMOS tech. In a word, they are awesome. You will not need headphones or bluetooth speakers if you are watching serials on this phone. They are extremely loud and clear.  On the negative side, headphone experience is mediocre. Yes, the surround effect is noticeable but it gives an effect of listening music in a large hall, reducing its clarity. This phone's audio playback is not better compared to the Sony Ericsson Xperia mini (yes the 2011 phone !) or the Nokia Lumia 735 that I had earlier
  

  Software: Once it boots up and connects to wifi, it immediately starts updating the software which takes about an hour or so. Once that is done, it performs well with no heating or battery drain issues. (Android 5.1.1 is not updated though) Wifi and network connectivity is seamless. Haven't experienced any disconnections so far. There is only one issue though, when switching from Wifi to Mobile data, one of the processes stops working and you get a pop-up. That is irritating but not a show stopper as things continue to work as expected.
  
  Phone reception is normal with no call drops or anything.
  
  - World Clock widget is absent by default (World clock app is present), you have to download it from PlayStore.
  
  - Notifications, even if disabled, wont disable for certain apps like Whatsapp or Skype
  
  - LED notifications cannot be disabled, and the LED does not blink, it stays on. Only two colors for the LED: Green and Red.
  

  Battery: 2750 mAh battery is good if you are not a heavy user spending more time on the phone than the laptop. Best part is that it charges pretty fast with 1.5A charger (DOES NOT have fast-charging feature).  With moderate usage (4 to 5 calls totaling 30 mins, 20 minutes of gaming, 30 mins of browsing and fb/whatsapp check every 30 mins), it drops to 30% by the time you have your dinner.
  
  When playing videos, the drain is faster and having a charger nearby is recommended. I did not see any battery saver option in-built but there is a Battery Optimization app which optimizes applications running in background for battery saving. I enabled it for whatsapp only to find that there are certain times when you wont get messages until you open the app.
  

  Note: I don't download lots of apps and keep notifications limited to chatting apps and e-mails.
  

  Camera: Just about average, nothing breathtaking, gets the job done on birthdays, team lunches and impromptu events. . Focusing takes more time than a coffee machine in certain low light conditions. Avid photographers should keep their dslrs handy.
  

  Summary: If you are that type of a person who likes phone usage to be minimal but needs great experience while you actually use it (for whatever miinimum time), this is the right phone for you. I am not worried about the camera as I take my DSLR on most outings. People looking for excellent snappers should look above 7500 INR budget IMO.

column6: The Best Smart Phone For Technical Mature Users
column7:
I got this Lenovo Vibe K5+ [3+16 Gb] Silver Color for Rs 6,749 on BB Days Offer via SBI Card via my cousin. This was the best option available for this price. However I will not advise anyone to buy this at Rs 8,500 as better options are available. This Phone is worth only Rs 7,000/- I will highlight my uses for the phone. I am a NIL Gamer NIL Camera User. I needed just a Phone for Long Hours of Wi-FI Internet, 3G Internet Access on the Go, Whatsapp, Twitter, E-Mails and productive work and especially typing via Wireless Keyboard Mouse. I also wanted to Honour technology & Inventors. For this the phone suited me perfectly. Also I had sentiment for the Lenovo Brand as my 1st laptop of 2009 still working is a Lenovo which has not given a single trouble till date. This is my first smartphone bought after much deliberation as last year during this same time I missed Micromax Canvas Xpress 2 thrice for Rs 5,499/- on BB Days. I am still viewing it's Box Opening and Test Videos.
  

  Pros:
  

  1-Full HD Screen 441 PPI No ghosting no shadow.
  

  2-USB OTG Support, works perfectly with Logitech USB Wireless Keyboard K230+Wireless Mouse M235 with Nano Receiver+USB Pen Drive ! Bought KB+Mouse with this Phone !
  

  3-Removable User Replaceable Battery
  

  4-Dedicated SIM Slots & Memory Card Not Hybrid One's
  

  5-Multi Apps do not hang or slow down the phone which is a must, At all times 2 Gb Ram is Free for user.
  

  6-No Hanging on long hours on Wi-Fi Internet or 3G.
  

  7-Upon 1st Boot there was a system update of 57 Mb after which there was no heating or
  
  hanging problem faced even once since 6th October 2016, I Rcvd the phone on 5th October 2016 night.
  

  8-No Heating on regular use or battery charging.
  

  9-Very Quick Battery charging from 5% to 100% in 90 Minutes
  

  10-Very useful screen Guard and Back Cover given rather than cheap quality headphones.
  

  Cons:
  

  1-The Battery for the first three charges was draining rapidly despite the fact that I uninstalled useless apps and installed DU Battery Saver App from Playstore.
  

  2-On 1st boot itself I uninstalled McAfee Security which was a huge Ram+Battery Drainer. But certain built in Apps like Chrome, Google Hangouts, Music, Pictures and other useless apps cannot be uninstalled only disabled. They continue to hogg space.
  

  3-Now after this Battery lasts for 15 hours on continuous usage, of Wi-Fi and on standby 18-20 hrs.
  

  4-USB OTG Pen Drive can be read only via Smartphone formatted file system. It does not read NTFS Pen Drives which work on PC's & Old Tablets. So one dedicated pen drive is needed to copy files from phone to PC.
  

  5-Like K3 Note it does not have double tapp screen to wake up, for which i installed a Android Apk from download.techdiscussion.in. This will prolong the life of power button.
  

  6-No Gorilla Glass or else this Phone Package would have been complete for me.
  

  7-I would have been happy, if this phone unlike others had a separate Charging PIN & separate OTG Micro USB Socket.
  

  So overall it was an excellent and splendid purchase for Rs 6,749 and I have no regrets as it served my purpose. I use the smartphone only for OTG Internet Access and not as my primary SIM or Calling no.
  

  I would ask all to opt for this phone if battery life, camera and gaming are not main considerations for superior technology considerations at the correct price.

column3: Lenovo Vibe K5 Plus (Dark Grey, 16 GB)
column7:
First of all FlipKart delivery was very prompt... Hats off to FlipKart services....
  

  Now moving to the product Lenovo's Vibe K5 Plus is really a value for price... I am writing this review after the use of 3 months...
  
  I was going to order Xiome Redmi 3S, but due to its unavailability I moved on to my 2nd best choice Vibe K5 Plus and ordered this with an SBI offer of 10% discount & flat 500 Rs OFF...
  
  So this phone cost me only 7,200...
  

  There is no headphones in the box, but instead lenovo provided a thin scratch gaurd & a cheap hard back cover...
  
  I would recommend you to use a good quality glass gaurd...
  

  As far as the phone is concerned, It has superb looks... Back panel looks really classic and fills very good in hand... Back panel grip is worst. Phone is light weight, but it can easily sleep out from your hand if you are careless handler... Overall built quality is superb...
  

  Screen is best in class.... Its really sharp and crispy... You can't see any pixelation... Colour are little bit dull... Brightness is sufficient...
  

  Dolby Atmos speakers are also rocking... But they are placed very close to each other reducing their surrounding effect... But it is still acceptable... Headphones output is also good...
  

  Camera is not as bad as reviewed by some guys... It may produce blur images if there is even a small hand shake with capturing photo... I have compared it with 13 MP of Redmi 3S and I found very small differences in quality... Camera hardware is good perhaps it has firmware with bad optimisation... Flash is powerfull enough...
  
  Front camera is also average... Produces blur images offenly in low light condition but acceptable for outdoor selfies in daylight...
  

  Battery backup is really worst... 2750 mAh battery powering its full HD display with Dolby powered speakers and Snapdragon 616 processor does not last for more than 6 hours even with moderate 4G Internet use...
  
  If you are a lightweight user and don't perform any battery intensive operations daily, then this battery can be acceptable... Those who wants continues use of Internet, play heavy games, etc etc then trust me this phone is not made for you...
  
  Charging with 1500 mA charger is fast enough... Charges from 10% to 99% in maximum 2 hours...
  

  There was overheating issue in this phone when its software was un_updated.. After an OTA update of 61 MB heating issues were solved... It still heats a lot during heavy gaming,  online video streaming, watching VR movies, or anything that may require heavy processing power... But for moderate use it works fine with moderate heating of back pannel... It is common in almost every smartphone in this price range...
  
  After another OTA update of 46 MB, I got VoLTE capability too...
  

  Snapdragon 616 octacore processor coupled with 3GB of RAM works fine... No hanging problem encountered yet...
  

  Vibe UI is really boring and default apps like Contact book, Dialler, File Manager are designed very congested and in each of them  you perhaps find bugs... I hope they will provide any better UI updates to their customers soon...
  

  It has given a LED notification light with only two colors Red for charging and Green for all notifications... Toggle switches on the Notification panel is non-customiseable and badly designed... It don't even has any toggle for Hotspot, USB Tethering and Reading mode... Touch keys are given with haptic feedback but don't have any back light...
  

  Other hardware like microphone, proximity,  notification LED, touch keys, earpiece, volume & power key are nice and well designed...
  
  Only its vibrator is too weak... You can hardly feel its vibration in pocket while ridding bike... But thanks to its powerfull Dolby speakers... At max volume they can ring and vibrate sufficiently to get the incomming call notified even in heavy traffic noise...
  

  Finally, considering all these minor cons along with its Crispy 5 inch fullHD display, Dolby Atmos, Snapdragon 616 processor with 3GB RAM at this nice price tag... Lenovo Vibe K5 Plus worth value for money...
  
  But don't forget about its insufficient battery backup and overheating issues before placing an order...
  

  I am not so happy but quite satisfied with this good looking smartphone...!

column3: Lenovo Vibe K5 Plus 3 GB (Gold, 16 GB)
column7:
It is a brilliant phone for the price. 3 GB memory handles most of the tasks thrown at it. It can handle most games like Asphalt etc.
  

  The audio output is good, but Dolby Atmos, when activated, just adds another dimension to the output through headsets. There are no headsets in the package, so it would be good to invest in a good headset like Senheiser or SkullCandy if you really are passionate about music. (You can buy a Bose, but why you'd buy this phone if you could afford a Bose is beyond me) For normal listeners, a good branded headset like Philips should work well.
  

  Camera is good for most situations, though you need to wait a wee bit for it to get the focus right at the point you want. I guess all the others who have given this camera a bad rating are professional experts who need the power of high end cameras in their phones.
  

  Now to the point of overheating. The updates that are downloaded when the phone connects to the internet handle that completely. The phone did not overheat even without the updates, so I assume the phone was updated before it was shipped. However it is a good practice to update the phone regularly. Minor heating when playing games for more than an hour is expected, so no surprises there.
  

  Now the only drawback I found was the lack of protective glass, either Dragon glass or gorillaglass on the screen. Given the propensity of phones to fall, it would be good to invest in a tempered glass cover. The package also includes a plastic back cover that fits the phone well and does not add to its bulk. Again, good practice to keep that cover on.
  

  Some suggestions: use an antivirus, a cleaner app and add a SD card in the expansion slot. That should keep it rocking for a long time.
  

  I think most of the complaints on this site are either out of immaturity or impatience. This is a great phone for the price and I would definitely recommend it.

column3: Lenovo Vibe K5 Plus 3 GB (Gold, 16 GB)
column7:
A real value for money product.
  

  Greetings to all the users of Lenovo Vibe K5 Plus users, confused buyers and review seekers.
  

  Today i have sincerely tried my best to give an honest and practical review of the phone based on my usage for the past 25 days. Enough has been said about its pros and cons. By now you must have learnt them by heart by just going through the numerous reviews here itself as well as on other sites so i will not be getting in to those details. I would just add that the phone performs AS ADVERTISED. If you keep your expectations at a practical level, you will not be disappointed. Now let us look in to some issues reported by users and try to logically understand them:
  

  - Yes, it does not come with an earphone but just by comparing the price of the product with its hardware specs and features, it feels justified that the company could not provide an earphone in order to cut costs and set such an unbelievable price for such a good product. I got this phone for around Rs. 6,200 under exchange.
  

  - The display is superb. The colours feel vibrant. Pictures are lively. Texts are crisp. It is an absolute delight to look at the screen. Sunlight readability is decent. I did not face any difficulty even when the sun was straight above my head and reflecting directly off the phone's screen.
  

  - Charging from 0% to 100% was achieved in about 2 hours and 15 minutes with the phone kept on along with 3G.
  

  - I use the phone for calling, chatting, web browsing, listening to music and use other utility apps. The battery lasts for around 18-20 hours which is pretty good. The good part is as the battery level decreases, the phone seems to be consuming lesser power.
  

  - Now the most talked about issue   Heating. The phone comes with an aluminium body. As we all know aluminium is a good conductor of heat and with all the powerful hardware embedded in a slim body like this, it is bound to get warm. But it never got uncomfortably hot. We should also keep in mind that the skin on our palms is more sensitive to heat as compared to rest of the body. Further, most of us have been using plastic bodied phones with less powerful hardware till now, hence for first time users it might feel as if it heats up too much but trust me after using it for some time you will get used to it. The heat generated by the device is normal.
  

  - Yes, Dolby ATMOS equalisers cannot be set to our own preferences beyond a certain level, but a third party equaliser app will solve this problem.
  

  - The processor supports VoLTE but an OTA update is awaited to activate the same. Lenovo officials have confirmed about the update but the release date is not yet confirmed. Vibe K5 Note recently got a similar update. So we are in the queue.
  

  - I have talked to Lenovo Customer Care personnel and they have said that Android 6.0 update has been confirmed by the company but again the release date is yet to be confirmed.
  

  - I am not a photography buff so i refrain from giving any comments on the camera quality.
  

  In a nutshell, it is a value for money product and will not disappoint the buyer. If you are wondering why i did not give it a 5 star rating then that is because giving it 5 stars would mean it is perfect but as we all know, nothing is perfect. Perfection is a myth. I would have given it 4.5 stars if i could.
  

  Last but not the least, a special thank to Flipkart and the seller for delivering the product on time and in perfect mint condition. I felt as if it had been directly delivered from the factory.

column3: Lenovo Vibe K5 Plus 3 GB (Gold, 16 GB)
column6: Classy product in beginning then it becomes worse
column7:
In the beginning:
  
  Awesome phone. Value for money. No other reputed brand is giving so much specs at this price. Many have complained about the heating issue. But there is an update waiting for us. As soon as I installed the update it solved the issue. I played many heavy games like asphalt8, nfs no limits, subway surfers and found no lag at all. Even in multitasking while switching from one app to other it was quick. No doubt at all about the display and sound quality as the screen display is FHD and it has dual speakers with dolby atmos. It has all the necessary sensors. We can experience theatremax and vr apps with a vr headset. The theatremax feature is nice. It feels like watching a movie in a theatre even though we are at home. I was glad to find a back cover already fitted with the phone. The design of the phone looks premium. Although people might think it has only 2750mah its battery backup is good as it does not consume much battery. It does not come with a headphone but that is fine for me as the price is not that high and also the company given headphones are always just of average quality and we always prefer to get a better headphone. The camera is not upto the mark under low light condition but still its acceptable. The little low performance of the camera is negligible when you have so many specs and features that too at a reasonable price.
  
  Very fast delivery. Was delivered within 3days and was packed nicely.
  

  But after 3-4 months:
  
  Everything started becoming worse. Battery started draining quickly. Discharging rate was faster than charging rate. Touchscreen response started becoming worse. GPS quality became worse. Lag and Heating issues started increasing. Although the specs are good but the quality of materials used is very poor.

Lenovo's popular low-cost K-series has had a bit of an identity crisis over the past year. The popular low-cost K3 Note was succeeded by the Vibe K4 Note (Review), which didn't really fit into the same category, and then by the Vibe K5 Plus (Review), which was more of a return to K-series roots. Priced at just Rs. 8,500, the Vibe K5 Plus actually addresses a lower-cost section of the market than the Vibe K4 Note, and is a viable competitor to similarly priced devices from Xiaomi, Asus, Coolpad, Honor, and others.
  
  Now, Lenovo has decided to introduce two K5 variants in India; the premium K5 Note, and the budget Vibe K5. The former gains the familiar 'Note' suffix, it looks like it's going to be a higher-end all-metal device when it launches. On the other hand, the Vibe K5 is a stripped-down, low-cost phone designed to appeal to those on a tight budget, and this is the device we're taking a closer look at today.
  
  lenovo_vibe_k5_lowerfront_ndtv.jpg
  
  Look and feel
  
  The new Vibe K5 looks pretty much identical to its sibling, the K5 Plus. It has exactly the same style and is available in the same three colours: silver, gold, and grey. We don't mind this at all because we were quite happy with this design the first time we encountered it. It isn't the slickest phone around, but it definitely doesn't look low-end.
  
  The body is all plastic, except for a thin plate of metal in the middle of the rear. This helps the phone feel sturdy, for what it's worth. A shiny chrome ring runs around the front and protects the screen from scratches when the phone is placed face-down on a table. We're a little concerned that the finish will wear off, especially at the corners and edges, but a simple case will help it stay looking fresh.
  
  lenovo_vibe_k5_rear_ndtv.jpg
  
  Grip is pretty good, and one-handed usage is easy. The Vibe K5 is light with gently curved edges on the back. Sadly, the three Android navigation buttons below the screen are not backlit. The Micro-USB and 3.5mm ports are on the top, and the power and volume buttons are on the right. A status LED lights up in the upper right corner of the front when you have a notification.
  
  In addition to the primary camera and flash, you'll see twin speaker grilles and a Dolby logo on the back. Unlike other phones which have symmetrical grilles for looks alone, the Vibe K5 actually does have stereo speakers, which is interesting for this price segment. The rear and sides are a single shell which comes off entirely, and you'll see a removable battery, two Micro-SIM slots and a microSD card slot underneath.
  
  lenovo_vibe_k5_upperfront_ndtv.jpg
  
  Specifications and software
  
  The Qualcomm Snapdragon 415 SoC is quite a step down from the Snapdragon 616 in the Vibe K5 Plus. The screen resolution is also a step down, from 1080p to 720p. However, most other things are exactly the same across both models. There's still 2GB of RAM and 16GB of storage plus microSD card support. You get 4G support on either SIM, plus Wi-Fi b/g/n and Bluetooth 4.1. The rear camera resolution is 13 megapixels and the front camera can take 5-megapixel shots.
  
  The battery has the same 2750mAh capacity and it should actually last a bit longer on this phone thanks to the less demanding screen and processor. We pointed out in our review of the Lenovo Vibe K5 Plus that it lacked things that some of its competition offers such as a fingerprint sensor or an Infrared emitter, and while this model doesn't have them either, it isn't as big a deal considering the price difference.
  
  lenovo_vibe_k5_right_ndtv.jpg
  
  You get Android 5.1.1 running a custom skin by Lenovo called VibeUI, which isn't very different from stock Android. It's neat and clean with everything where you'd expect it to be. We noted with the Vibe K5 Plus that there was no dedicated app drawer, but this phone does have one. It's possible that Lenovo added this functionality in an update due to feedback.
  
  Just like with the Vibe K5 Plus, the capacitive Recents button on the front panel has actually been mapped to the deprecated Android menu function, which is only relevant on Lenovo's custom homescreen now and serves no other purpose. You have to long-press this button to see the app switcher.
  
  lenovo_vibe_k5_top_ndtv.jpg
  
  Pre-loaded apps include Amazon, Evernote, GameStore, McAfee Security, Route 66 maps, Tap the Frog, Truecaller, Twitter, UC Browser, and WeChat, which are probably useful but uninstallable if you prefer. There's also Lenovo's SHAREit, a Dolby control app, Lenovo Companion for updates and diagnostics, and Theme Center for customising your phone's looks.
  
  Performance
  
  While probably good enough for most people's casual usage, we found the Vibe K5 just a bit sluggish. There were momentary delays when launching apps, pulling up menus, and just generally getting things done. The display has poor viewing angles, taking on a definite tint when you aren't looking at it head-on. Brightness and colours are okay,

column7:
I have been using the Samsung Galaxy E5 for the last one and half years I grabbed the offer of Flipkart to exchange it for Lenovo Vibe K5 Note without thinking much. Added benefit I got 10% off  using SBI debit card to pay for it. Total bill was approximately 8.2k with Ant VR which comes at a price of  500 if baught togather with the this phone. The very first difference I felt  was the weight and slimness. My E5 was noticeably lighter (148g) and slimmer than K5 Note (165g without any cover or protective layer). It may take some time to adjust. But one handed operation is easier on K5 despite being a 5.5 incher whereas my old one was a 5incher. Overall qualuty of Lenovo is at best adequate and looks neither stunning nor bad. It has metal back compared to plastic used in E5; still quality wise E5 occupy a better place; but it is just my mind or hand telling so; other may say different. Lenovo's front camera produces decent selfies ; same as Samsung; just bigger. There are gestures to capture photoes without touching the sets in both phones. Rear camera is a huge upgrade. Galaxy's 8MP used to take okayish pictures  but those looked very pleasant on Samsung's 720p ~326ppi Super Amoled screen with stunning colores although a bit saturated. Lenovo Vive K5 Note delivers reallycommendable outcome from it's 13MP as good as Xiomi's new offering in the same and with phase detection auto focus or PDAF it takes very less time to focus on subject. Photoes or videos on it's full hd 1080p 400+ ppi LCD looks real still no match for Super Amoleds. So I would say screen is somewhat downgrade for me. Speaker sound is loud and clear and creates pleasant vibration in air. All I can say it has nice ring to it. With headphone (I use Samsung E5's headphone as there was no headphone in the Lenovo's package) it is noiseless hifi out put with support from Dolby Digital.
  
  Android Marshmallow 6.0 runs on K5.

  I am happy with this mobile and that's all matters.

In my case with Wifi ON, around 2 hrs of calls and 3 hours of chatting, with in between internet and multimedia usage the battery reduced from 100% to 44% in 11 hours.
  
  8. Fingerprint Sensor - Unlocking time is quite ok, but not very fast.
  
  9. Signal Strength and call Quality - Awesome.
  
  10. RAM - 4GB is excellent, it will run huge number of apps in background without any lag.
  


  Cons:
  

  1. Slippery though it has a metal finishing it may slip from your hand any time. Better use with the cover.
  
  2. Though fingerprint sensor works fine, it is failing to recognize one or the other time.
  
  3. Hybrid slot - definitely a disappointment
  
  4. Single LED flash
  
  5. Feels bit bulky and heavy.
  
  6. Software - with series of bloatware of which most cant be uninstalled.
  


  As per my view, if you are camera lover and looking for more storage then you should have a look around.   * Fingerprint Scanner: the scanner is blazing fast. The position is perfect for using your index finger to unlock. I tried it using 5 different fingers it without any hiccup.
  

  * processor: the Helio P10 64- bit is not the latest but is very smooth and amazingly powerful. I was bit sceptical about it at the beginning, but am really blown up by the processing speed and it's power handling whatever thrown at it. Heating is comparatively very minimal.
  

  * Clear voice calls: this is a neglected aspect but K 5 note has done a great job here. The calls are crystal clear without any distortion. VoLTE is an added functionality that is the future of the mobile networks soon. So you can be future proof with the device.
  

  *Heavy gaming: not an issue with the fast professor and ample RAM of 4GB. Can play any graphic intensive game easily. Also the device doesn't get heated up to an uncomfortable level. So that is a plus.
  

  * Sound quality speaker and headphones: the speaker is satisfactory. The quality is excellent. Theatermax technology with Dolby Atoms system makes it totally different from the other phones. The sound through headphones are really amazing and crisp. Use good quality headphones, I use sennheisers gives a great output. Love the sound output through the headphones.
  
  *Sensors: all major sensors present in the device.
  

  Sshhhuu. A lot of pros.. Let's check out the cons now.
  

  * Charging time: there is fast charge 1. But sadly that is not fast compared to today's standards where many devices are coming around with fast charge option. The battery is huge so it would really take a long 2 to 3 hours to charge from 0-100%.
  
  * Camera: The Camera in this segment is one of the best (except Mogo G Camera). The Quality is great in ample lighting conditions. But little bit struggle in low light and complex lighting conditions. LED flash gives a better exposed picture in darkness. Hope it gets a little better with software updates. That can be done and it is also expected as the sensor is quite good.
  
  * No water resistance: yeah that is a must now a days owing to the changing trends in the smartphones usage. You can live without it but it's good to have it .
  
  *Still this cons doesn't take away the crown of best value for money smartphone in the market at present.

  * Make the camera performance a little better especially in low light conditions. Hope that is coming soon in the next updates.

Writing this review after using this phone for almost a month.
  
  A pretty decent phone. Unlike previous phones in the Lenovo K-series the  K5 has no heating problems at all.  I've been constantly using it on 4G data 24/7 and never faced heating issues. considering I'm a heavy user and multi-task a lot.
  
  Secondly user interface is smooth,  no lags on average day to day usage. Ram management is smooth. At any given point of time atleast 800 mb ram is free even with many apps running.
  
  Camera isn't the best but it'll get you through the day. It's almost stock Android,  minimalistic,  simple and fast,  almost zero shutter lag. The front cam is nice though,  selfie lovers will be pleased {please don't compare it to a freaking iPhone}.
  
  Regarding gaming, it can handle most games thrown at it. Heavy duty games like dead trigger, mortal combat,  asphalt etc can cause slight lag and heating.. But unless you're not a hard core gamer this phone is pretty good and will easily play through your common games like candy crush or subway surf or whatever it is you want to play.
  
  The interface is good and intelligent and Lenovo had added a lot of nice functionality, making your interface enjoyable and handy .. Finger print scanner is a bit over sensitive, so you need to watch that. But it's effective.  Screen quality is decent,  you can adjust the saturation as you want. Capacitive buttons are back-lit.  Screen to body ratio is really nice. And the Lenovo trademark Dolby atmos sound feature is excellent. You can really make out the difference in sound quality when comparable to other phones .VR mode is also nice. Lenovo pushed all the right buttons this time.
  
  Final verdict.
  
  Pros :-
  
  good price point value
  
  Decent front camera, fast camera app.
  
  Efficient ram management
  
  No heating  (as far as I've tested)
  
  Excellent sound output.
  
  Cons :-
  
  the phone doesn't really have a con .. Except maybe for the over sensitive finger print scanner.
  

  It doesn't really excel in anything in particular  but It's got everything needed for above average usage.
  
  Media junkies will love this phone for the  sound quality and the VR functionality.
  

  If you want an excellent camera in this price range try out Huawei honor 5c or 5x.
  
  If you're more focused on gaming go for letv or moto.
  

  But if you want everything above average ,  in  a handy package go for this one.

  Build Quality - Metal body. So the heat spreads all the time and you will feel a little warm. However, i didnt faced any overheating issues. Please note that phone will heat a bit while charging. 4.5/5
  

  Software Quality - The main part of lenovo i like is their almost original Android UI with some essential tweaks. I did faced some hang sometimes, like once every week. Restarted the phone and everything was fine. 4.5/5
  

  Fingerprint Sensor - This is my 3rd Fingerprint Sensor phone and the worst i have ever seen. Please do not buy this phone if 1. This is your 1st Fingerprint phone and 2. Fingerprint is your one of the primary reasons to buy this phone. The problem is in registering the Fingerprint, it dosenot show you the areas it is registering so you end up with a wrong Fingerprint data - which means you may unlock the phone with a specific angle or area of your finger.
  
  Also, holding the Fingerprint sensor sends multiple feedbacks - so if you are doing it wrong, holding the sensor will treat that you did it wrong 20 times and will not let you use the sensor for a while. 0/5
  

  Summing up, 3/5 .

column7:
Well I am writing this review after 3 weeks of use. Initially i was little confused between K5 Note & Mi-Max. But due to unavailability of Mi-Max, i landed up with K5 Note.
  

  overall I would say decent performance with Airtel-4G. Internet stuff & media activities are good. Call Quality is good in moving conditions.
  
  Camera i must say very good. Selfie pics are having very good clarity. rear camera is also doing decent job at this price segment. In low light conditions, pics are just ok. not so good.
  

  But Battery life could have been better. With 3500 mAH battery i expected to last the charge at least one day. But this is not the case.
  
  If you use 4G/3G for 15 mins then at least at least 7 to 10 % of battery charge drop noticed. Two of my colleagues have also bought same variant & they also found the same issue. If you use the device for continuous active internet then charge will is going down faster.
  

  in case of gaming. experience is good with heavy games like Nova, Unkilled etc. But when playing basic games like Candy crush then also battery is going down like anything. Here also it is going down almost 1% per 2 minutes.
  

  Below are the summarized Pros & Cons:
  

  Pro:
  
  Great look, Big screen
  
  Good for media & internet.
  
  Display is good & bright.
  
  Finger print scanner is working good.
  
  3G/4G connectivity is working good. Call Quality is good in basement & also in moving Lift. (With Airtel)
  
  Android Marshmallow is better performing.
  
  Not so heavy weight which is good.
  
  Camera is very good. Specially front camera clarity is very good.
  


  Cons:
  

  Battery for Sure is very bad (other buyers are complaining about same). With moderate use of internet it wont last for 24 hours.
  
  Sound should be better. Speaker sound is not so loud.

  VoLTE support is not there! this is a big con looking at the GIO SIM launch. (Lenovo says it is there but not enabled. this doesn't make any sense)

  Hybrid Sim: New feature but not good for them who want to use dual sim & micro SD too.

Added benefit I got 10% off  using SBI debit card to pay for it. Total bill was approximately 8.2k with Ant VR which comes at a price of  500 if baught togather with the this phone. The very first difference I felt  was the weight and slimness. My E5 was noticeably lighter (148g) and slimmer than K5 Note (165g without any cover or protective layer). It may take some time to adjust. But one handed operation is easier on K5 despite being a 5.5 incher whereas my old one was a 5incher. Overall qualuty of Lenovo is at best adequate and looks neither stunning nor bad. It has metal back compared to plastic used in E5; still quality wise E5 occupy a better place; but it is just my mind or hand telling so; other may say different. Lenovo's front camera produces decent selfies ; same as Samsung; just bigger. There are gestures to capture photoes without touching the sets in both phones. Rear camera is a huge upgrade. Galaxy's 8MP used to take okayish pictures  but those looked very pleasant on Samsung's 720p ~326ppi Super Amoled screen with stunning colores although a bit saturated. Lenovo Vive K5 Note delivers reallycommendable outcome from it's 13MP as good as Xiomi's new offering in the same and with phase detection auto focus or PDAF it takes very less time to focus on subject. Photoes or videos on it's full hd 1080p 400+ ppi LCD looks real still no match for Super Amoleds. So I would say screen is somewhat downgrade for me. Speaker sound is loud and clear and creates pleasant vibration in air. All I can say it has nice ring to it.   Good rear camera. Great front camera. The front camera pictures are great but the videos look slightly blurry at times and I hope Lenovo fixes it with a software update. Footages from the rear camera are good but Lenovo has to optimize the focusing algorithms with a software update. Low light performance is average but you can't ask for more for this price.
  

  The display is laminated but it doesn't have the wow factor certain laminated displays have. The icons don't pop out of the screen as much as you'd see on an iPhone 6S :P. Don't get me wrong. The display is very good and pleasant to look. The colours are great and everything looks very crisp. The touchscreen is pretty slick and very responsive too.
  

  The fingerprint sensor works just fine but I wish it could be calibrated a bit more for greater accuracy but it's a software thing anyway.
  

  The audio from the rear firing speaker is pretty awesome. It's not tinny at all, has a good bass response and it's pretty loud too. The audio from the 3.5mm jack is just amazing. It's pretty flat but it's crystal clear and loud enough. You can hear each of the notes hover around your ears.
  

  No. Lag. Observed. At. All. This is perhaps the most important thing for me. The four gigs underneath does it's job just fine.
  

  Being a power user, I tweak around a lot and I'm pretty confident that this phone can get through anything you throw at it without breaking a sweat. I don't give a shit about hardcore gaming (which it does manage quite well to a certain extent) so I'm good to go with a Helio P10. This phone has pretty decent hardware. Let's hope Lenovo does the same job on the software.
  

  (Will update after the update. Pun intended. :P)
  

  Update: I've been using this for around a week now.
  

  The good things:
  

  The phone is pretty good. It's quite snappy. It doesn't hang much. Doesn't heat up very fast. Handles pretty much everything you throw at it. Apps and games work just fine. Audio quality is awesome both from the loudspeaker and the 3.5mm jack. Battery lasts a day with average use. Front camera is truly great for selfies! Rear camera performs well for outdoors photos.
  

  The bad things:
  

  It's cumbersome to get a good image from the rear camera. Outdoor shots are very good. Indoors, the focus fails sometimes for macro shots and the images lack sharpness and detail. But some other times, the images turn out to be just fine. Video is average outdoors and not very impressive indoors. Front video is average outdoors and very noisy indoors.
  

  The camera can perform way better if it gets some good software optimization. The 300MB update I received did nothing in my experience.
  

  Some apps like Google Camera are not listed in the PlayStore. I tried installing it manually but it crashes the moment I run it. Come on Lenovo! We need good software!

Flipkart experience:
  
  Delivered within 3 days.

  The phone:
  
  The lenovo packaging was great. Unboxing was a nice experience in itself.

  They also provide and OTG adapter in the box.
  
  The phone looks and feels great.
  


  Pros:
  

  Battery : 5100mAh lasts for 2 to 3 days of moderate use.
  
  Fast charge : Proprietary 24W charger charges the 5100mAh behemoth in just 2 hrs. So 2 hrs of charging and you're good to go for 2 days.
  
  Ultra power saving mode : Will make your phone last for a couple of weeks without charging. Might come in handy. Never had to use it in the 3 weeks I used it.
  

  Great value for money(at 13.5k for 3/32GB variant)
  

  Display : Full HD super AMOLED is simply too beautiful and also  reduces power consumption
  
  Protection : Corning Gorilla Glass 3
  

  Speakers : Mono at the base. Really loud and good quality sound as well.
  

  Build quality : Solidly built. Buttons feel good to the touch. 2.5D curved class also makes it a great looking phone altogether. Does not feel heavy despite the huge battery capacity.
  

  NFC : Has NFC support. Not too many phones have NFC support in this price segment.
  

  Fingerprint sensor : Super fast and accurate. Can also be used to replace functions of the 3 buttons home,  back and app switcher.
  

  Features : Loads of handy features such as tap on screen to awake, double click volume button to quickly  capture a photo while phone is still locked, etc.
  

  OS : Marshmallow out of the box which is upgradable to Nougat. Lenovo has maintained the near stock Android experience with the vibeUI as a secondary launcher.
  

  Performance : QS625 with the 3GB RAM  gave seamless lag free performance and more than decent gaming performance. Memory management  is good with quick app switching.

  Hybrid SIM slot : Would have been better with a dedicated memory card slot.

It's been a while I was thinking of changing my old lenovo A680. Not necessarily as a gadget freak's upgrade, but it became necessary after using it for three years. In android phones all that matters to me is its battery back up. That A680 also had a better back up compared to rest in its range. I personally got upto 23 hours, with one roaming sim always in it. I'd say that was decent for a phone costing just 6000. But it had the worst ever mobile camera in all android phones, somehow for my own good perhaps kept me away from harbouring that narcissistic selfie clicking habit. Now present job engagements made me to feel like I need larger storage and longer battery back up. So I was eyeing on this product since a long time, reading people's reviews here, except those which simply judge the product by thanking Flipkart. Flipkart must get thanks, but that is not the product's review. Anyway, the reviews sent me to the judge's dilemma. I have to buy two of it, if I buy at all, but with different requirements. So kept on searching for other mobiles also. And like Hyundai cars, nothing seems to be absolutely perfect, but roughly made all rounder, and you need to choose from that. The other person needed one basically for camera, and I needed basically for longer back up. So finally with much hesitations we settled down for Lenovo P2, remaining loyal to Lenovo once again. Now the experiences:
  

  You'd like:
  

  1. Battery back up.
  
  Yes, I'd agree with rest of the reviewers. At present it is the best you can get. And that too for merely 15,000 budget. Or else you can wait for some other future phones. And power banks are worthless. They simply give an uninterrupted supply, but don't charge up to full efficiency. Forget the powerbank now. With heavy use too, it should return with you back to home at the end of the day's business. My personal best is 36 hours.
  

  2. Rapid Charging.
  
  First day I charged it full, and it took surprisingly short while. Earlier Lenovo phones had bad reputation for taking long and longer time. My previous two lenovo phones (A516 and A680) used to take 4-5 hours with their kit chargers. But later I used to charge them with a Sony adapter which reduced the time to two and a half hours. But this one, no one can complain.
  

  3. Touch
  
  Smooth as butter, not greasy at all. I m just wondering what we had to do with the old resistive touch screens and how responsive this screen is even to a tenderest touch.
  

  4. Snapdragon chipset.
  
  Don't know much about technicalities of the processors, but one thing for certain from the experience that snapdragon is better than the mediatek. Earlier experienced heavy heating up issues with mediatek phones, which was not there with my old HTC phone with snapdragon. But these days HTC too comes up mostly with mediatek. That thing just keeps product costs a bit cheaper, but users will soon get the heat, literally.
  

  5. RAM
  
  You have the option for going to 4GB or order the 3GB. Choice is definitely yours. I had opted for the 3GB and with some basic apps, like VLC media player (because it plays anything and everything), whatsapp, facebook and its messenger, office suit, and dictionary I still have 50% available. Gamers have the option to spend another 2000 bucks for one added gigabyte. It should not be an issue for you folks when you have ample memory to do anything.
  

  6. Power saver button
  
  There is a factory set power saving button. You need not to get confused how to set your power saving plans. Lenovo has already decided it for you.
  

  7. No extra post buying cost
  
  You'll get the back cover, OTG, and the screen guard. These are the things people fumble for.
  

  8. For patriots, it's made in India
  


  You'd be Okay with:
  

  1. Camera.
  
  Far better than previous Lenovo phones. At least it saved me from carrying my bulky cameras along. Many features are there like manual focusing, ISO setting etc, which would serve the purpose to the extent till you want to be a good photographer with a real camera. photography and videography is good, okeyish to me.
  
  But, there is a but. I had recently tried the videography with this phone. I was yet to be accustomed with its settings though. Shot outdoor, in a railway station yard, having variable lighting. Video quality was awesome, BUT the noise cancellation is poor. Wind whipping just somehow appeared in the sound although that was barely audible to my own ears. So apparently providing with Carl Zeiss lens, it still somehow managed to keep track with the Lenovo tradition of spoiling the camera.

Lenovo P2 is definitely one of the best smartphones available in the budget. One can opt for redmi note 4 but here are some points which I consider better then the competitor.
  

  1. The better screen-- Yes! I am sure that one can definitely fall in love with this screen as it is having a super AMOLED full HD display. This produces deeper blacks and more punchier  colors and a great viewing angles.
  

  2. The better battery-- This mobile comes with 5100mAh battery which is more then redmi note 4 and as per my use, a single charge is lasting more then 1.5 days. I am a moderate user who surf more, whatsapp, instagram, facebook and a very less gaming(mostly none). There is a dedicated switch on the left side of the mobile which is think is great way to save that last juice in the battery before one rush to home, but would be great if that switch is allowed to customize.
  

  3. Fingerprint scanner-- This sensor is very fast and works like a charm. Coming from redmi note 3 I noticed no much improvement in the speed but i can definitely say that the detection is very accurate, unlock in most cases unlike redmi N3.
  

  4. Built-- The built is great and feels study. Metal body design gives a premium feel and chamfered edges provides much premium feel. The bottom firing speaker is loud enough and this comes with only one speaker but not two.
  

  5. Android-- This comes with almost stock android and the experience is very smooth. Out of the box you might get android M but immediately it will be upgraded to android 7 so thus supporting almost all the features of Nougat like split screen and better apps management etc.
  

  6. Camera-- The camera is the weakest point in this mobile but not the worst. You can have a good snap in great lighting conditions but the sensor suffers in low lights. There is an option called manual mode which is not great but helpful for some one who doesn't like auto mode(exposure correction is very poor). Forget about HDR, its just an option to wipe the tear of the customers. I am not a selfie guy and couldn't complain about front cam, but can say that its good for video calls.
  

  7. Performance-- This comes with SD 625 and the performance is great for day to day use and quick app switching. 625 is not so power hungry and i feel that its a major aspect why this mobile is lasting so long on a single charge even on heavy usage. 3GB ram is okay, with only 700mb to 1gb of free ram on normal use. Even though the mobile is running smooth.
  

  8. Fast charger-- we get a lenovo's custom fast charging adapter which is very quick in charging the massive battery and its a standard micro USB port(not type-C). I ran a small test by charging the mobile from 10% to cent and it took 75mins. Its interesting quick and this is what i like the most in this mobile. No heating issues till date even on heavy usage(not gaming) or charging. The charger might get a little hot(not as hot as iron box) but that's not an issue.
  

  9. In the box-- We get a transparent case fitted along with a screen guard(not tampered) in the box. Also a OTG is given which lenovo says that one can charge other mobile with this mobile(haven't tried yet).
  

  10. Notification light-- Yes this is having a notification light at the top right next to the front camera. Can produce blue, red, and violet/pink(not sure about this color).
  

  11. Sim Slot/Memory card Slot-- This comes with hybrid tray which means you can either plug in two SIM cards or one SIM or one memory card. However one can get 32gb internal storage out of which you will be getting approx 23gb memory to use. But if one wants to carry extra space for entertainment then they should definitely sacrifice their secondary SIM.
  

  Cons>>>
  
  1. The power button and the volume rocker feels a little loose.
  

  2. camera is not that great for one who like to click pics.
  

  3. Late android updates. Running on Android 7.0 (security patch is dated to Feb 2017, which is almost 5 months old).
  

  Verdict>>
  

  if one is looking for a mobile which lasts long on single charge with eye catching display, premium build quality and smooth android OS experience then they can definitely go with Lenovo P2 without second thought. Don't expect desired mobile cases to be available for this device, you will struggle a bit for them. Would give 9/10 for the device(-1 for camera).

Lenovo P2.. Double the battery power
  

  Design (9/10)
  
  Build quality is very good.It feels very solid in hand. Whole metal construction gives p2 a very     premium look. But the power button and the volume rockers are slightly wobbly. I know this is only nitpicking.
  

  Display (9.5/10)
  
  P2 have a full hd super amoled screen with pixel density of 401 ppl. Screen size is 5.5 inch with wide viewing angles and very good sunlight legibility. Screen is easily visible in harsh sunlight. Amoled panels do have the tendency to show over saturated colors. But to overcome this problem Lenovo provided the color mode option in display settings. Where you can select between two options normal or vibrant. In normal mode colors are more close to real. And 2.5D curved glass makes display more beautiful. There is glass protection too and it is Corning Gorilla Glass 3. If you want to apply screen protector then you can find one in the box itself.
  

  Camera (7/10)
  

  Hmm..This is the first weak point i found in this device. Well, camera in low light is bad. Although there are few modes like art nightscape,panorma,pro,hdr, fast motion and slow motion. Fast motion and slow motion we can use while video recording.Video quality is good in sun light but there is constant focus hunting.In night and indoors you will find noise and softness in videos and pictures. While using night mode you can reduce noise but at the cost of sharpness and details. In day light pictures comes out good but sometimes with blown out colors. Videos are also not well stabilized. In short camera in low light is bad and in day light is above average in terms of price to performance ratio.Results from front camera are also same as primary camera.Front camera is 5 mp and primary camera is 13 mp with which you can shoot up to ultra hd videos.
  

  Software and performance (9/10)
  

  Well it is running on Android 6.0 which is upgradeable to Android 7.0. I haven't updated my device to nougat yet.There is 32 gb internal memory and 3gb ram on my device. On first boot you get 2.8 gb of total ram and 23.87 gb of internal memory.There is a support for dual apps but it is half baked because you can use this feature in default launcher. UI is very smooth and very close to stock rom. There is not lot of bloatware and you can easily uninstall pre installed apps. There are on screen navigation buttons which you can easily hhide and use button on botton which have finger print scanner , as one key solution. Finger print scanner is fast and accurate. Usb otg is also supported. In short performance is lag free and very good.
  

  Battery (100/10)
  

  Yes i haven't mistyped above.Battery life is awesome and i got 13 hours of screen on time in three days of usage. If you are a heavy user then also you will need charger after two days.The charger provided in the box is rapid charger. Time taken to charge from 0  to 100  is 2 hours and 35 minutes.And this is very good because battery is of 5100 mah capacity.
  

  Gaming (8/10)
  

  Chipset is snapdragon 625 and gpu is adreno 506. Most of the games played well without lag. I played dream league soccer and it ran without any issue. But i found minor frame drops after playing the game for 25 minutes. But there are not any heating issues.
  

  Sound and Audio quality (8/10)
  

  There is a single speaker at the bottom. The speaker is adequately loud, infact i have seen the loudest single speaker  in p2 after xperia xa ultra. Sound output from speaker have some kind of bass in it. Audio quality from ear phoes is very good, with deep bass. But i suggest to use some better quality earphones because the ear phone provided in the box are bad in quality but atleast ear phones are there, thanks to Lenovo for that. But there is not dolby atmos support, but don't worry! Audio quality is loud, clear and clean.
  

  Verdict (8.5/10)
  

  P2 is power house in terms of battery. I got it for rs. 11249. In this price it is much better product than redmi note 4. Flipkart delivery was very good so kudos for that. Performance of this device is also very good. We can say everything in this phone is good or excellent except camera which is pretty average at its best.

I have been using this phone for past 20 days and trust me it is one of the best phones i have ever used.
  

  Battery life: You all have already heard many things about it. I was going from Cochin to Delhi by train (48 hours). I watched 3 movies on Jio cinema, made few hours of calls, listened to songs from Jio Music (for around 6 to 8 hours), browsed through Facebook and Whatsapp and watched some Youtube. The phone was still at 10% when I reached Delhi.
  

  Build Quality : My brother is using Xiaomi redmi note 4 which is also a metal build phone. However the touch and feel of both these phones are quite different. In comparison P2 seems to be more premium and refined.
  

  Screen Quality : Hands down, the best display you can get on a phone under 20,000 INR. The quality is comparable to that of one plus 3.
  

  Audio Quality : My mother is having Lenovo A6000 plus which has dual dolby audio speakers. This phone has a single speaker without any dolby enhancements. However, the phone easily matches the volume levels of A6000 plus and surpasses it in terms of quality and depth. The audio through the headphone jack is also top notch. I have skullcandy earphones and JBL headphones and the phone can power them quite easily.
  

  Performance : The phone is powered by snapdragon 625 which delivers outstanding battery life but doesn't deliver similar results in terms of performance. Don't get me wrong, the phone is almost as fast and smooth as a oneplus 3 in daily usage and the memory management is also excellent, however sometimes the transition animations get a little choppy and the phone freezes every time for a couple of seconds when I hit the clear all notifications button. This can be a software issue as well and can be fixed in future updates, however we all know the mischievous Lenovo and its history of software updates (by the way I am currently running android N update on the phone and not hoping any other update for my phone in its lifetime). As far as gaming performance is concerned the phone delivers and hits way above its belt. No complaints in this department. This performance combined with superb screen and speaker quality gives one of the best multimedia experience I have ever experienced.
  

  Camera Quality : On paper the phone has a 13 MP sony shooter with 4K video recording capability. The phone gives good quality photos in day light. The selfy camera is 5MP and is good when the amount of is abundant. The camera app provides manual mode and some predefined artistic HDR and night  modes. These modes help in capturing the shots in low light. The photos taken in low light look very artificial, even though the details are well captured. The front camera is no good in low light. We usually take photographs outdoor in broad sunlight, and the  pics turn out very good there. In low light condition the pics are good provided you keep the phone steady (its mandatory). As far as night shots are concerned, the phone really struggles, however I haven't seen any device taking good photos in such scenario. My sister has an iphone 6s and even it's camera struggles in night.
  

  Verdict : I was in a need of a great multimedia device with ever lasting battery life. This phone stands up tall for every need of mine. Lenovo also provides a screen guard and a hard case for the phone. Moreover the box pack also includes micro USB to USB converter and the phone even supports my 2TB WD hard drive. The in box eraphones are not good, but they are in the box and can be used as a back up in case  your primary earphones die. The phone also has native support for VR theatremax mode as well. Hands down,this is the best phone you can get under 20,000 INR provided a little compromise on the camera front.
  
  If you want your manufacturer to provide a timely update (at least for security patches) or you want to buy a phone only for shooting pictures, then this is not the phone. However if you want a good overall phone which excells in multimedia and battery department and gets the job done in the camera department and don't really bother whether you are running the latest version of android or the latest security patch, then this is the phone for you.
  

  As far as the shopping experience with Flipkart is concerned, it never dissapoints. The phone was delivered on the second way after the order was placed.

I have been using this phone for a week now. Here are my initial impressions and review...
  

  I bought Lenovo P2 Graphite Grey 3GB ram variant for Rs11499 after exchanging my mi 3, during the summer sale.
  

  PROS:
  
  1)Good build quality. Overall the phone is made up of metal with precision cut speaker and mic grills at the bottom. On the back side also the phone has a metal body with Lenovo branding (subtle) but the top and bottom are plastic mainly, as they act as antenna receptors. The phone feels very nice to hold. Very dense feeling. The 2.5D curved glass with premium metal build is overall a great combo. Only complaint is that the power button feels a bit wobbly.
  

  2)The battery. As I expected the battery being the major feature of this phone, is exceptionally good. The phone lasts for 3 days with light usage and 2 days with heavy usage. But I normally manage to get around a full day and a half day with 20% battery still left(that is games, YouTube, mail, texting, call, downloads ,surfing ,editing, camera usage , recording and what not.). I feel that a phone with a good battery is a must and I have no complaints in this regard. The phone also has a dedicated battery saving hardware button.
  

  3)The display. It is absolutely amazing. A mid budget phone having a super amoled display with deep blacks, warm tones and high contrast colors is damn pretty to look at. This is my first phone with a super amoled display and I feel that it is the prettiest display I have seen yet. I wake the phone just to gaze at the screen. The colors are not accurate as it has high contrast but I like it that way. It also has a natural color mode in settings menu if one does not like the high contrast display.
  

  4)Rapid charge. There's nothing to say about this  feature. This phone supports rapid charge v3 that is not the same as quick charge v3 or dash charge. Rapid charging is proven to be better than dash  charging. It can easily bring the battery level up from 15% to 60% in 40 min(keep in mind as it is a 5100mah battery so dont compare battery levels with other phones). It can charge the phone completely in 1hour 40 mins. It has 5v 7v and 12v channels. So charging your phone in a brief period is not an issue with this phone.

It's been a while I was thinking of changing my old lenovo A680. Not necessarily as a gadget freak's upgrade, but it became necessary after using it for three years. In android phones all that matters to me is its battery back up. That A680 also had a better back up compared to rest in its range. I personally got upto 23 hours, with one roaming sim always in it. I'd say that was decent for a phone costing just 6000. But it had the worst ever mobile camera in all android phones, somehow for my own good perhaps kept me away from harbouring that narcissistic selfie clicking habit. Now present job engagements made me to feel like I need larger storage and longer battery back up. So I was eyeing on this product since a long time, reading people's reviews here, except those which simply judge the product by thanking Flipkart. Flipkart must get thanks, but that is not the product's review. Anyway, the reviews sent me to the judge's dilemma. I have to buy two of it, if I buy at all, but with different requirements. So kept on searching for other mobiles also. And like Hyundai cars, nothing seems to be absolutely perfect, but roughly made all rounder, and you need to choose from that. The other person needed one basically for camera, and I needed basically for longer back up. So finally with much hesitations we settled down for Lenovo P2, remaining loyal to Lenovo once again. Now the experiences:
  

  You'd like:
  

  1. Battery back up.
  
  Yes, I'd agree with rest of the reviewers. At present it is the best you can get. And that too for merely 15,000 budget. Or else you can wait for some other future phones. And power banks are worthless. They simply give an uninterrupted supply, but don't charge up to full efficiency. Forget the powerbank now. With heavy use too, it should return with you back to home at the end of the day's business. My personal best is 36 hours.
  

  2. Rapid Charging.
  
  First day I charged it full, and it took surprisingly short while. Earlier Lenovo phones had bad reputation for taking long and longer time. My previous two lenovo phones (A516 and A680) used to take 4-5 hours with their kit chargers. But later I used to charge them with a Sony adapter which reduced the time to two and a half hours. But this one, no one can complain.
  

  3. Touch
  
  Smooth as butter, not greasy at all. I m just wondering what we had to do with the old resistive touch screens and how responsive this screen is even to a tenderest touch.
  

  4. Snapdragon chipset.
  
  Don't know much about technicalities of the processors, but one thing for certain from the experience that snapdragon is better than the mediatek. Earlier experienced heavy heating up issues with mediatek phones, which was not there with my old HTC phone with snapdragon. But these days HTC too comes up mostly with mediatek. That thing just keeps product costs a bit cheaper, but users will soon get the heat, literally.
  

  5. RAM
  
  You have the option for going to 4GB or order the 3GB. Choice is definitely yours. I had opted for the 3GB and with some basic apps, like VLC media player (because it plays anything and everything), whatsapp, facebook and its messenger, office suit, and dictionary I still have 50% available. Gamers have the option to spend another 2000 bucks for one added gigabyte. It should not be an issue for you folks when you have ample memory to do anything.
  

  6. Power saver button
  
  There is a factory set power saving button. You need not to get confused how to set your power saving plans. Lenovo has already decided it for you.
  

  7. No extra post buying cost
  
  You'll get the back cover, OTG, and the screen guard. These are the things people fumble for.
  

  8. For patriots, it's made in India
  


  You'd be Okay with:
  

  1. Camera.
  
  Far better than previous Lenovo phones. At least it saved me from carrying my bulky cameras along. Many features are there like manual focusing, ISO setting etc, which would serve the purpose to the extent till you want to be a good photographer with a real camera. photography and videography is good, okeyish to me.
  
  But, there is a but. I had recently tried the videography with this phone. I was yet to be accustomed with its settings though. Shot outdoor, in a railway station yard, having variable lighting. Video quality was awesome, BUT the noise cancellation is poor. Wind whipping just somehow appeared in the sound although that was barely audible to my own ears. So apparently providing with Carl Zeiss lens, it still somehow managed to keep track with the Lenovo tradition of spoiling the camera.
  


  You won't like:
  
  1. No dolby atmos.
  
  2. Below average earphones. It matters to many.
  


  Final verdict:
  
  All the above advantages should outnumber the disadvantages. Price:Features correlation definitely puts it on the top. I'll suggest this phone if your budget is within 20k. You'll never regret.
  

  And I forgot to thank Flipkart, it's available only here.
