Lenovo P2 is definitely one of the best smartphones available in the budget. One can opt for redmi note 4 but here are some points which I consider better then the competitor.
  

  1. The better screen-- Yes! I am sure that one can definitely fall in love with this screen as it is having a super AMOLED full HD display. This produces deeper blacks and more punchier  colors and a great viewing angles.
  

  2. The better battery-- This mobile comes with 5100mAh battery which is more then redmi note 4 and as per my use, a single charge is lasting more then 1.5 days. I am a moderate user who surf more, whatsapp, instagram, facebook and a very less gaming(mostly none). There is a dedicated switch on the left side of the mobile which is think is great way to save that last juice in the battery before one rush to home, but would be great if that switch is allowed to customize.
  

  3. Fingerprint scanner-- This sensor is very fast and works like a charm. Coming from redmi note 3 I noticed no much improvement in the speed but i can definitely say that the detection is very accurate, unlock in most cases unlike redmi N3.
  

  4. Built-- The built is great and feels study. Metal body design gives a premium feel and chamfered edges provides much premium feel. The bottom firing speaker is loud enough and this comes with only one speaker but not two.
  

  5. Android-- This comes with almost stock android and the experience is very smooth. Out of the box you might get android M but immediately it will be upgraded to android 7 so thus supporting almost all the features of Nougat like split screen and better apps management etc.
  

  6. Camera-- The camera is the weakest point in this mobile but not the worst. You can have a good snap in great lighting conditions but the sensor suffers in low lights. There is an option called manual mode which is not great but helpful for some one who doesn't like auto mode(exposure correction is very poor). Forget about HDR, its just an option to wipe the tear of the customers. I am not a selfie guy and couldn't complain about front cam, but can say that its good for video calls.
  

  7. Performance-- This comes with SD 625 and the performance is great for day to day use and quick app switching. 625 is not so power hungry and i feel that its a major aspect why this mobile is lasting so long on a single charge even on heavy usage. 3GB ram is okay, with only 700mb to 1gb of free ram on normal use. Even though the mobile is running smooth.
  

  8. Fast charger-- we get a lenovo's custom fast charging adapter which is very quick in charging the massive battery and its a standard micro USB port(not type-C). I ran a small test by charging the mobile from 10% to cent and it took 75mins. Its interesting quick and this is what i like the most in this mobile. No heating issues till date even on heavy usage(not gaming) or charging. The charger might get a little hot(not as hot as iron box) but that's not an issue.
  

  9. In the box-- We get a transparent case fitted along with a screen guard(not tampered) in the box. Also a OTG is given which lenovo says that one can charge other mobile with this mobile(haven't tried yet).
  

  10. Notification light-- Yes this is having a notification light at the top right next to the front camera. Can produce blue, red, and violet/pink(not sure about this color).
  

  11. Sim Slot/Memory card Slot-- This comes with hybrid tray which means you can either plug in two SIM cards or one SIM or one memory card. However one can get 32gb internal storage out of which you will be getting approx 23gb memory to use. But if one wants to carry extra space for entertainment then they should definitely sacrifice their secondary SIM.
  

  Cons>>>
  
  1. The power button and the volume rocker feels a little loose.
  

  2. camera is not that great for one who like to click pics.
  

  3. Late android updates. Running on Android 7.0 (security patch is dated to Feb 2017, which is almost 5 months old).
  

  Verdict>>
  

  if one is looking for a mobile which lasts long on single charge with eye catching display, premium build quality and smooth android OS experience then they can definitely go with Lenovo P2 without second thought. Don't expect desired mobile cases to be available for this device, you will struggle a bit for them. Would give 9/10 for the device(-1 for camera).

  P2 have a full hd super amoled screen with pixel density of 401 ppl. Screen size is 5.5 inch with wide viewing angles and very good sunlight legibility. Screen is easily visible in harsh sunlight. Amoled panels do have the tendency to show over saturated colors. But to overcome this problem Lenovo provided the color mode option in display settings. Where you can select between two options normal or vibrant. In normal mode colors are more close to real. And 2.5D curved glass makes display more beautiful.   Camera (7/10)

Fast motion and slow motion we can use while video recording.Video quality is good in sun light but there is constant focus hunting.In night and indoors you will find noise and softness in videos and pictures. While using night mode you can reduce noise but at the cost of sharpness and details. In day light pictures comes out good but sometimes with blown out colors. Videos are also not well stabilized. In short camera in low light is bad and in day light is above average in terms of price to performance ratio.Results from front camera are also same as primary camera.Front camera is 5 mp and primary camera is 13 mp with which you can shoot up to ultra hd videos.

  Well it is running on Android 6.0 which is upgradeable to Android 7.0. I haven't updated my device to nougat yet.There is 32 gb internal memory and 3gb ram on my device. UI is very smooth and very close to stock rom. There is not lot of bloatware and you can easily uninstall pre installed apps.   Gaming (8/10)

I have been using this phone for past 20 days and trust me it is one of the best phones i have ever used.
  

  Battery life: You all have already heard many things about it. I was going from Cochin to Delhi by train (48 hours). I watched 3 movies on Jio cinema, made few hours of calls, listened to songs from Jio Music (for around 6 to 8 hours), browsed through Facebook and Whatsapp and watched some Youtube. The phone was still at 10% when I reached Delhi.
  

  Build Quality : My brother is using Xiaomi redmi note 4 which is also a metal build phone. However the touch and feel of both these phones are quite different. In comparison P2 seems to be more premium and refined.
  

  Screen Quality : Hands down, the best display you can get on a phone under 20,000 INR. The quality is comparable to that of one plus 3.
  

  Audio Quality : My mother is having Lenovo A6000 plus which has dual dolby audio speakers. This phone has a single speaker without any dolby enhancements. However, the phone easily matches the volume levels of A6000 plus and surpasses it in terms of quality and depth. The audio through the headphone jack is also top notch. I have skullcandy earphones and JBL headphones and the phone can power them quite easily.
  

  Performance : The phone is powered by snapdragon 625 which delivers outstanding battery life but doesn't deliver similar results in terms of performance. Don't get me wrong, the phone is almost as fast and smooth as a oneplus 3 in daily usage and the memory management is also excellent, however sometimes the transition animations get a little choppy and the phone freezes every time for a couple of seconds when I hit the clear all notifications button. This can be a software issue as well and can be fixed in future updates, however we all know the mischievous Lenovo and its history of software updates (by the way I am currently running android N update on the phone and not hoping any other update for my phone in its lifetime). As far as gaming performance is concerned the phone delivers and hits way above its belt. No complaints in this department. This performance combined with superb screen and speaker quality gives one of the best multimedia experience I have ever experienced.
  

  Camera Quality : On paper the phone has a 13 MP sony shooter with 4K video recording capability. The phone gives good quality photos in day light. The selfy camera is 5MP and is good when the amount of is abundant. The camera app provides manual mode and some predefined artistic HDR and night  modes. These modes help in capturing the shots in low light. The photos taken in low light look very artificial, even though the details are well captured. The front camera is no good in low light. We usually take photographs outdoor in broad sunlight, and the  pics turn out very good there. In low light condition the pics are good provided you keep the phone steady (its mandatory). As far as night shots are concerned, the phone really struggles, however I haven't seen any device taking good photos in such scenario. My sister has an iphone 6s and even it's camera struggles in night.
  

  Verdict : I was in a need of a great multimedia device with ever lasting battery life. This phone stands up tall for every need of mine. Lenovo also provides a screen guard and a hard case for the phone. Moreover the box pack also includes micro USB to USB converter and the phone even supports my 2TB WD hard drive. The in box eraphones are not good, but they are in the box and can be used as a back up in case  your primary earphones die. The phone also has native support for VR theatremax mode as well. Hands down,this is the best phone you can get under 20,000 INR provided a little compromise on the camera front.
  
  If you want your manufacturer to provide a timely update (at least for security patches) or you want to buy a phone only for shooting pictures, then this is not the phone. However if you want a good overall phone which excells in multimedia and battery department and gets the job done in the camera department and don't really bother whether you are running the latest version of android or the latest security patch, then this is the phone for you.
  

  As far as the shopping experience with Flipkart is concerned, it never dissapoints. The phone was delivered on the second way after the order was placed.

  Pros:
  
  1.    5100Mah bigger battery which almost last 2 days for me.
  
  2.    Super AMOLED display (made by Samsung) which produces colours more punchy and vibrant which looks too good and provides better feeling compare to IPS LCD panel. And LED display is power conservative so it will increase phone's battery life also.
  
  3.    5.5-inch display which provides the better experience during watching videos and movies.
  
  4.    This phone based on Snapdragon 625 chipset so I do not find any lag and hang issues during heavy gaming.
  
  5.    Snapdragon 625 is well known as balanced and power efficient chipset so it will help to save phone's battery life also.
  
  6.    This phone is available in two RAM variant 3GB/4GB. I have used 3GB variant which is sufficient for normal day to day to use. I think 3gb variant is value for money.
  
  7.    Quick charging support which is another advantage of this phone. My phone almost took 1hr and 40 min to charge 0 to 100%.
  
  8.    The design of this phone is good. Not much heavier not very light. I feel good in the hand.
  
  9.    NFC support which I have not used till now.
  
  10.    A single Louder speaker so you don't have to worry if you work in a noisy place.
  
  11.    Audio quality is very good Lenovo done very good job in speaker section.
  
  12.    Cellular connectivity is too good. I have used Jio sim from the fast day.
  

  Cons:
  
  1.    A poor camera which is not expected from a 13500+ device where others Smartphone did a better job in this price range.  I don't say that camera is very poor but I would expect much better. Camera performance is good in daylight condition(outdoor shooting) but during the indoor shooting in low light condition, the camera has to start struggling up and capturing noisy photos.
  
  2.    Software problem, I have noticed app crashing and screen freezing issues when I update this phone marshmallow to nougat. I think it will be solved in next regular software bugs update.
  
  3.    Not dual speaker and Dolby is not supported. But the audio quality is good.
  
  4.    Another small cons unavailability of tempered glass protector due to 2.5D curved display which is not deal breaker.

Now I have used new Lenovo P2 with marshmallow and no such issues observed so I will recommend to every buyer who wants to buy this phone please be careful and don't update your phone marshmallow to nougat. I would suggest updating the software of this phone from Marshmallow to Nougat after 3-4 months I think Lenovo will solve this bugs with the software update.
  



  Conclusion: If you want to buy a phone which battery last almost two days, if you like LED display, if you would like to buy a good performance device then go for Lenovo P2 and if the camera is the highest priority then go for other Smartphones in this price range.

I have been using this phone for a week now. Here are my initial impressions and review...
  

  I bought Lenovo P2 Graphite Grey 3GB ram variant for Rs11499 after exchanging my mi 3, during the summer sale.
  

  PROS:
  
  1)Good build quality. Overall the phone is made up of metal with precision cut speaker and mic grills at the bottom. On the back side also the phone has a metal body with Lenovo branding (subtle) but the top and bottom are plastic mainly, as they act as antenna receptors. The phone feels very nice to hold. Very dense feeling. The 2.5D curved glass with premium metal build is overall a great combo. Only complaint is that the power button feels a bit wobbly.
  

  2)The battery. As I expected the battery being the major feature of this phone, is exceptionally good. The phone lasts for 3 days with light usage and 2 days with heavy usage. But I normally manage to get around a full day and a half day with 20% battery still left(that is games, YouTube, mail, texting, call, downloads ,surfing ,editing, camera usage , recording and what not.). I feel that a phone with a good battery is a must and I have no complaints in this regard. The phone also has a dedicated battery saving hardware button.
  

  3)The display. It is absolutely amazing. A mid budget phone having a super amoled display with deep blacks, warm tones and high contrast colors is damn pretty to look at. This is my first phone with a super amoled display and I feel that it is the prettiest display I have seen yet. I wake the phone just to gaze at the screen. The colors are not accurate as it has high contrast but I like it that way. It also has a natural color mode in settings menu if one does not like the high contrast display.
  

  4)Rapid charge. There's nothing to say about this  feature. This phone supports rapid charge v3 that is not the same as quick charge v3 or dash charge. Rapid charging is proven to be better than dash  charging. It can easily bring the battery level up from 15% to 60% in 40 min(keep in mind as it is a 5100mah battery so dont compare battery levels with other phones). It can charge the phone completely in 1hour 40 mins. It has 5v 7v and 12v channels. So charging your phone in a brief period is not an issue with this phone.
  

  5)The software. Nearly stock with a few Lenovo tweaks which are good. Minimum bloatware which can be uninstalled easily. Out of the box it came with marshmallow but immediately got an update for nougat(android v7.0). snappy software with good battery and ram optimization.
  

  6)Speakers. Although it is not a pro  but it is quite loud even louder than my msi laptop speaker. It does not distort much. But sometimes it may distort depending on the frequency. I like the sound of the speaker overall. Others may not agree.
  

  7)Fingerprint senor is nice. 8/10 times it gets the job done. Quite fast to unlock. Can also act as software navigation buttons.
  

  8)4G volte, expandable storage, led notification, nfc, otg support, reverse charging.
  


  CONS:
  

  1) The camera. Although not worse but it is not upto the mark. Can get decent photos under good lighting. Has a manual mode for focus and exposure and all. Yet the camera both front and back falls quite short. Photos are average. Under lowlight are disasters. Macro under good lighting is good. Can get the job done with instagramming and social networking. Video rec supports fhd and  4k. Slow mo mode is also present. Lenovo tweaks make the camera a bit better. Overall a satisfactory experience.
  

  2) Power button is a bit wobbly . although not an issue still it bothers me a lot.
  

  3) Does not support wifi ac bands. Does not have ir blaster. (although these are not necessary for a budget phone - I feel)
  

  4)Hybrid slim slot so either u can have 2 sims or one sim and 1 memory card at a time. A combination of both the options are not present.
  


  This is my early review and initial impressions. I may update my review after spending some more time with my phone. Overall i am very satisfied with Lenovo and this phone. Exceeded my expectations truly. The pros easily outweigh the cons. Lenovo is finally starting to make good phones. I am so pleased with this phone i am even considering to buy the P3 instead of one plus or m phones in the future. I might have missed some points but those i mentioned are the most important to me.

After using for  2.5 months
  
  Here's what I honestly feel about this phone.
  

  Pros:
  

  1. Super AMOLED Display : 10/10
  

  This display is 5'5 inch and is  best among all other brands at this price range even under 20k phones. Just look at the phone in dark night. One thing I love the most that you have Night mode option (update to Android 7.0 Nougat? ) Screen gets a bit yellowish.
  
  doesn't stress the eyes.
  

  2. Speakers : 9/10
  

  Speaker is loud man and have a little bass effect too. Which makes it perfect for listening songs.
  

  3. Battery  : 10/10
  

  Battery Man. It's huge. 5100mAh. goes easily for 2-3 days on normal to heavy use.
  
  Maximum Screen on time use on my phone was - 13:48 hours.
  
  Lowest Screen on time was - almost 9 hours ( I used DU recorder along with Playing Asphalt 8. continuously. )
  
  Average Screen on time is 11-12 hours.
  

  4. Sleek and Premium Design : 9/10
  

  Despite having a huge battery the phone is very slim.. but bit slippery.. looks much better than Redmi Note 4 and other phones under 20k. Grey /Graphite combination is best.
  

  5. Sanpdragon 625 Processor : 8 /10
  

  This processor is smooth and fast.. runs every highly graphics games available at playstore.
  
  Best Games I've played so far:
  

  Asphalt 8: Airborne
  
  Modern Combat 5
  
  Mortal Kombat X
  
  The Wolf Among Us. (Telltale Games)
  
  Space Marshals 2
  
  Major Mayhem
  
  LoneWolf
  
  Tentacles - Enter the Mind
  

  This is best at this price range. Yes, Redmi Note 4 and latest Tenor 10.Or G are having same processor too. But considering other things.. this beast beats them all.
  

  Maximum temperature hit 41 degrees Celsius.
  
  Average 37 dergrees Celsius. Both at body temperature.
  

  6. Fast Charging : 8/10
  

  It is supported by Qualcomms Quick Charger 3.0 which indeed charges really fast. Phone gets double flash whicle on Fast Charging mode. (Works only when phone's screen is locked. or Phones power off.)
  
  But Sometimes the charger and phone gets heat up while charging (depends on various factors) and could reach upto 44 degree Celsius.
  

  Fastest charging time 0-100% - 1 hour 28 minutes
  
  Slowest charging time 0-100% while on bit usage - 2 hours 15 minutes.
  
  Remember 5100 mAh battery.
  

  7. Sensors : 10/10
  

  It has total 16 sensors. Install My Device App.
  

  Some important sensors are :
  

  Gyroscope sensor - Supports Virtual Reality
  
  Magnetometer
  
  NFC - Near Field Communication - Got the logo in the back.
  
  Still waiting to use in future
  

  8. Notification Led : 10/10
  

  It's so beautiful and amazing to have Notification Led light.. whenever you get a notification you have different colours for different  app notification.
  

  9. Ultra Power Saving Mode button : 9/10
  

  Man.. It's absolutely a bonus. Its located on the left side of the phone. Does the work pretty good. It actually closes all the background apps and gets the phone in a parallel universe where   it only allows you to  have basic options to use like Call, Messages, Calculator, Calendar. Of course it shows time.too.
  

  10. Front Fringer Print Sensor Button : 10/10
  

  Woah. Fringerprint Sensor button in the front. Which also acts as back/home/multitasking button. It's not the fastest but it's fast.
  
  Hold tap to multitasking. Single tap to back. Double tap to home screen I guess.?
  

  Also you get the option to hide On screen Navigation Button. Honestly, I never use on screen navigation buttons.
  

  So Guys. there are other amazing  features too.
  
  You can change Display/Text size to smallest. It looks good.
  
  Also you have Microscreen feature.
  
  Dual Apps.
  
  Multi Windows. Just go on multitasking windows- hold on to one Windows, Swipe up. there you go! ;)
  
  Also you have option to see Data transfer speed. just check the settings.
  
  Damn.. I said it all.
  

  Now.. let's come to the bitter part of this phone:
  
  You guys know it.
  

  1. Camera : 7/10
  

  Yes it's the biggest weak piont of this phone. but wait... that is only for low and indoor light. otherwise it shoots just fine.
  
  Pictures taken at morning or during day time is actually really  good.
  
  You just have to turn on the smart mode in Camera. You know?!
  

  2. Storage : 7/10
  

  Storage could have been better atleast 64 GB.
  

  3. Hybrid Sim Slot.  7/10
  

  It's actually gets confusing at first when you first put in the Sim cards. Both Sim slots supports 4G Volte. but only One Sim use Volte at a time. Also you can't insert External micro SD  when using both Sims in slots. Otherwise it works great.
  

  Overall 87.69/100.
  

  Some basic tips :
  

  1. Use a complete Dark wallpaper for Lockscreen and Homecreen.
  
  I think it looks simply amazing.
  
  2. Set the icons and Display/Fonts size to smallest. Display settings.
  
  (not recommended to the  people with weak eyesight)
  
  3. Install QuickPic for Gallery.  Works really fast.
  
  4. Always use default Android Launcher.
  
  5. Hold on to the home screen , go to widgets, look for Lenovo weather. get it on home screen. Cool.
  
  6. Get a better screen protector. Buy it on TrinkShop(dot)com @250 rupees range.
  

  So far so good. This is the best phone for value.
  
  Go for it.

  Hardware: Fingerprint scanner is highly sensitive and efficient. 4gb ram really smoothens out the multitasking. Snapdragon 625 and adreno graphics gives a really smooth gaming experience.   Camera: I'm not a camera enthusiast myself but 13mp rear gives more that decent shots. Low light brings in noise. 5mp front pretty much serves seldom taken selfies and are more than just fine.
  

  Display: Super amoled display protected by Gorilla glass 3 is absolute pleasure to look at and reproduces colours  extremely well. I'm not a fan of amoled displays but HD videos can be enjoyed the way they were meant to be seen. 8pts!!
  

  Features: Quick charging is really appreciable and gives 0 to 90% charge in 90mins.
  
  VR mode works great.
  
  Quick snap (double tap vol to take quick snap directly from screen off)), knock to light,  dual app profiles all comes real handy in day to day access. 8pts!!
  

  Connectivity: BSNL 3g did give decent speeds. i tested reliance jio and works well. Having hybrid slot and only 32gb internal is a real pain. But using a hybrid sim adaptor like i did, solves that aspect. Wifi gives speeds as expected and the scanning range is really good. I'm able to connect to the hotel apartment on the other side of the road. Yayy.. Connecting to Bluetooth speakers also worked well and fine. 9pts!!
  

  Verdict: i, to be honest, was not a fan of Lenovo and was the last brand i would consider while investing my money. are you looking for a budget phone with features of a high end phone??does frequent charging slow you down??   It all depends on your needs.

column6: Excellent phone in this price range
column7:
I ordered this phone during the 10th anniversary sale period and got a bargain after exchanging my old phone. So let me break my review down into 2 parts:
  

  Pros:
  
  1. The battery: This is one thing which sealed the deal for me. 5100 mAh is no joke. I'm a moderate to heavy user, continuously using 4G, youtube and games. it easily lasted 2.5 days on a single charge. and for light to moderate users, it'll last even more. No other phone offers this kind of juice at this price. The fast charging also works like a charm. Be sure to charge it in a cool place. It'll charge itself from 1% to 99% in 1.5 - 2 hrs. Charging in a warm atmosphere will take its charging time up.
  

  2. The screen: The super AMOLED screen on this phone is nothing short of sensational. The quality and depth of colours is beyond what any phone offers at this range. AMOLED far outweighs the traditional IPS LCD in both color depth and picture quality ( having used IPS LCD display phone before). It is also more power efficient than IPS display.
  

  3. The processor: The processor (SD 625) works smoothly and has almost no lag whatsoever while playing games, streaming videos, multi tasking. The phone also has no heating issues while charging or while playing games. I bought the 4GB RAM model. But with this processor, even 3GB RAM is plenty for everyday tasks.
  

  4. The fingerprint scanner: The fingerprint scanner is an active fingerprint scanner. So just place a finger on it lightly and it unlocks itself. Quite smooth and easy to use.
  

  5. Nougat update: As soon as you connect your phone, it upgraded to Nougat (android 7). It became even smoother after the update and battery optimization became even better as the OS uses lesser power for apps. Also the vibe UI on the P2 gives a stock android like feel and doesn't eat up into the RAM and memory as on a redmi note 4.
  

  Cons:
  
  1. 32 GB ROM: Almost every phone offers 64 GB at this price point and lenovo should have done the same. I, being a moderate user could make use of the hybrid slot to run another sim and not a memory card but more memory is always welcome.
  

  2. Camera: Although, this is not a deal breaker, the camera quality (both front and rear) could've been way better. Lenovo's sister brand Motorola offers better camera with good low light performance on the G5 and why this hasn't been implemented by lenovo is anyone's guess. In daylight the 13 MP primary cam offers good clarity and sharpness. But low light pics take a hit due to noise and over saturation of colors sometimes. The front is a 5 MP and this is again a skimp by lenovo as most brands offer atleast 8MP front at this price point. Use cyanogen mod camera or any custom camera app like beautyplus or philm to take good pictures and selfies.
  

  3. Earphones: This is the one part where i was left flabbergasted. For a phone that costs 18k (for 4GB RAM), the earphones are ones similar to ones you get on entry level phones. They're made of plastic and do not offer as much clarity and bass as that of any other phone's earphones, leave alone ones like sony and sennheiser.
  

  4.
  

  So guys, this is my review after nearly a fortnight of usage. The pros of this phone outweigh the cons is what I feel and any user who wants battery life and loves to play games, watch movies and videos can blindly go for it as there is no other phone at this range offering some unique features the P2 offers. Cheers to all the new buyers !!!

Don't get me wrong K5 note is a really good device but at this price tag, it fails to do what it should do.
  

  -------
  
  PROS:
  
  -------
  
  1. Very simple and sleek design. (added pictures)
  
  2. Dolby atmos makes it one of the best sound smartphones in the market. Really loud and clear.

  7. 4G, Dual sim and MircoSD slot(up to 128GB).

  10. 13MP camera with Dual LED Flash.
  
  11. Matte type finish on the back makes a good grip on the phone.
  
  12. An excellent output from the 3.5mm jack, all you need is a good app like poweramp and pair of earphone.

  --------

  1. Heavily bloated, so many unnecessary apps some of them even can't be removed by a normal user. (Lenovo never thinks of user experience)
  
  2. I'm not a big fan of Mediatek processors but these days to cut the cost of devices companies have no choice left. If you are a heavy user might see some performance issues.

  4. Average quality pictures from the Camera.

  VR mode available

Footages from the rear camera are good but Lenovo has to optimize the focusing algorithms with a software update. Low light performance is average but you can't ask for more for this price.
  

  The display is laminated but it doesn't have the wow factor certain laminated displays have. The icons don't pop out of the screen as much as you'd see on an iPhone 6S :P. Don't get me wrong. The display is very good and pleasant to look. The colours are great and everything looks very crisp. The touchscreen is pretty slick and very responsive too.
  

  The fingerprint sensor works just fine but I wish it could be calibrated a bit more for greater accuracy but it's a software thing anyway.
  

  The audio from the rear firing speaker is pretty awesome. It's not tinny at all, has a good bass response and it's pretty loud too. The audio from the 3.5mm jack is just amazing. It's pretty flat but it's crystal clear and loud enough. You can hear each of the notes hover around your ears.
  

  No. Lag. Observed. At. All. This is perhaps the most important thing for me. The four gigs underneath does it's job just fine.
  

  Being a power user, I tweak around a lot and I'm pretty confident that this phone can get through anything you throw at it without breaking a sweat. I don't give a shit about hardcore gaming (which it does manage quite well to a certain extent) so I'm good to go with a Helio P10. This phone has pretty decent hardware. Let's hope Lenovo does the same job on the software.
  

  (Will update after the update. Pun intended. :P)
  

  Update: I've been using this for around a week now.
  

  The good things:
  

  The phone is pretty good. It's quite snappy. It doesn't hang much. Doesn't heat up very fast. Handles pretty much everything you throw at it. Apps and games work just fine. Audio quality is awesome both from the loudspeaker and the 3.5mm jack. Battery lasts a day with average use. Front camera is truly great for selfies! Rear camera performs well for outdoors photos.
  

  The bad things:
  

  It's cumbersome to get a good image from the rear camera. Outdoor shots are very good. Indoors, the focus fails sometimes for macro shots and the images lack sharpness and detail. But some other times, the images turn out to be just fine. Video is average outdoors and not very impressive indoors. Front video is average outdoors and very noisy indoors.
  

  The camera can perform way better if it gets some good software optimization. The 300MB update I received did nothing in my experience.
  

  Some apps like Google Camera are not listed in the PlayStore. I tried installing it manually but it crashes the moment I run it. Come on Lenovo! We need good software!

Well I am writing this review after 3 weeks of use. Initially i was little confused between K5 Note & Mi-Max. But due to unavailability of Mi-Max, i landed up with K5 Note.
  

  overall I would say decent performance with Airtel-4G. Internet stuff & media activities are good. Call Quality is good in moving conditions.
  
  Camera i must say very good. Selfie pics are having very good clarity. rear camera is also doing decent job at this price segment. In low light conditions, pics are just ok. not so good.
  

  But Battery life could have been better. With 3500 mAH battery i expected to last the charge at least one day. But this is not the case.
  
  If you use 4G/3G for 15 mins then at least at least 7 to 10 % of battery charge drop noticed. Two of my colleagues have also bought same variant & they also found the same issue. If you use the device for continuous active internet then charge will is going down faster.
  

  in case of gaming. experience is good with heavy games like Nova, Unkilled etc. But when playing basic games like Candy crush then also battery is going down like anything. Here also it is going down almost 1% per 2 minutes.
  

  Below are the summarized Pros & Cons:
  

  Pro:
  
  Great look, Big screen
  
  Good for media & internet.
  
  Display is good & bright.
  
  Finger print scanner is working good.
  
  3G/4G connectivity is working good. Call Quality is good in basement & also in moving Lift. (With Airtel)
  
  Android Marshmallow is better performing.

It may take some time to adjust. But one handed operation is easier on K5 despite being a 5.5 incher whereas my old one was a 5incher. Overall qualuty of Lenovo is at best adequate and looks neither stunning nor bad. It has metal back compared to plastic used in E5; still quality wise E5 occupy a better place; but it is just my mind or hand telling so; other may say different. Lenovo's front camera produces decent selfies ; same as Samsung; just bigger. There are gestures to capture photoes without touching the sets in both phones. Rear camera is a huge upgrade. Galaxy's 8MP used to take okayish pictures  but those looked very pleasant on Samsung's 720p ~326ppi Super Amoled screen with stunning colores although a bit saturated. Lenovo Vive K5 Note delivers reallycommendable outcome from it's 13MP as good as Xiomi's new offering in the same and with phase detection auto focus or PDAF it takes very less time to focus on subject.   Good rear camera. Great front camera. The front camera pictures are great but the videos look slightly blurry at times and I hope Lenovo fixes it with a software update. Footages from the rear camera are good but Lenovo has to optimize the focusing algorithms with a software update. Low light performance is average but you can't ask for more for this price.
  

  The display is laminated but it doesn't have the wow factor certain laminated displays have. The icons don't pop out of the screen as much as you'd see on an iPhone 6S :P. Don't get me wrong. The display is very good and pleasant to look. The colours are great and everything looks very crisp. The touchscreen is pretty slick and very responsive too.
  

  The fingerprint sensor works just fine but I wish it could be calibrated a bit more for greater accuracy but it's a software thing anyway.
  

  The audio from the rear firing speaker is pretty awesome. It's not tinny at all, has a good bass response and it's pretty loud too. The audio from the 3.5mm jack is just amazing. It's pretty flat but it's crystal clear and loud enough. You can hear each of the notes hover around your ears.
  

  No. Lag. Observed. At. All. This is perhaps the most important thing for me. The four gigs underneath does it's job just fine.
  

  Being a power user, I tweak around a lot and I'm pretty confident that this phone can get through anything you throw at it without breaking a sweat. I don't give a shit about hardcore gaming (which it does manage quite well to a certain extent) so I'm good to go with a Helio P10. This phone has pretty decent hardware. Let's hope Lenovo does the same job on the software.
  

  (Will update after the update. Pun intended. :P)
  

  Update: I've been using this for around a week now.
  

  The good things:
  

  The phone is pretty good. It's quite snappy. It doesn't hang much. Doesn't heat up very fast. Handles pretty much everything you throw at it. Apps and games work just fine. Audio quality is awesome both from the loudspeaker and the 3.5mm jack. Battery lasts a day with average use. Front camera is truly great for selfies! Rear camera performs well for outdoors photos.
  

  The bad things:
  

  It's cumbersome to get a good image from the rear camera. Outdoor shots are very good. Indoors, the focus fails sometimes for macro shots and the images lack sharpness and detail. But some other times, the images turn out to be just fine. Video is average outdoors and not very impressive indoors. Front video is average outdoors and very noisy indoors.
  

  The camera can perform way better if it gets some good software optimization. The 300MB update I received did nothing in my experience.
  

  Some apps like Google Camera are not listed in the PlayStore. I tried installing it manually but it crashes the moment I run it. Come on Lenovo! We need good software!

  - Incredible sound. Powered by Dolby Atmos, the phone speakers actually burst out more decibels than my laptop (which is a Lenovo with Dolby as well).
  
  - 4GB RAM is more than enough. Although only half of it will be available in most general situations, 2GB is still pretty solid.
  
  - (Contd.) Switching b/w apps, playing games, and interacting with the phone in general, is very quick.
  
  - The battery is a mammoth. Once charged, you can keep using the phone for 2-3 days, all while playing games, 24*7 WiFi, watching videos, and listening to music every once a while.
  

  CONS:
  
  - Grip: The phone's grip is not safe. It's got a metal body but with the same curves as a normal phone. In fact, I dropped the phone after a few hours of buying, right on my marble floor (nothing happened btw). It should've had a more edgy grip to support the metal body.
  
  - Heating: The phone, being metal, heats on the back cover very fast. Similarly, it gets cold very fast if you keep it away for a while, even if on your bed. Metal is more sensitive to temperature changes.
  
  - Space: 8GB is taken up by the OS (Android 6.0). It happens in all phones, so that's nothing too unique. You're only left with 24GB of space for your stuff.
  
  - Camera: Camera, let me say, is DECENT. It's not really a con in itself. But when compared to other phones of the 10k range, surely the K6 Power has lesser to offer. Nevertheless, the images are crisp and it's got pretty okay low-light photography power.
  
  - Lack of quick charge mode might also bug certain people.
  
  - The earphones with the phone are a pain.

  in case of gaming. experience is good with heavy games like Nova, Unkilled etc. But when playing basic games like Candy crush then also battery is going down like anything. Here also it is going down almost 1% per 2 minutes.

column6: Feature rich phone for the money
column7:
I have been using the Samsung Galaxy E5 for the last one and half years I grabbed the offer of Flipkart to exchange it for Lenovo Vibe K5 Note without thinking much. Added benefit I got 10% off  using SBI debit card to pay for it. Total bill was approximately 8.2k with Ant VR which comes at a price of  500 if baught togather with the this phone. The very first difference I felt  was the weight and slimness. My E5 was noticeably lighter (148g) and slimmer than K5 Note (165g without any cover or protective layer). It may take some time to adjust. But one handed operation is easier on K5 despite being a 5.5 incher whereas my old one was a 5incher. Overall qualuty of Lenovo is at best adequate and looks neither stunning nor bad. It has metal back compared to plastic used in E5; still quality wise E5 occupy a better place; but it is just my mind or hand telling so; other may say different. Lenovo's front camera produces decent selfies ; same as Samsung; just bigger. There are gestures to capture photoes without touching the sets in both phones. Rear camera is a huge upgrade. Galaxy's 8MP used to take okayish pictures  but those looked very pleasant on Samsung's 720p ~326ppi Super Amoled screen with stunning colores although a bit saturated. Lenovo Vive K5 Note delivers reallycommendable outcome from it's 13MP as good as Xiomi's new offering in the same and with phase detection auto focus or PDAF it takes very less time to focus on subject. Photoes or videos on it's full hd 1080p 400+ ppi LCD looks real still no match for Super Amoleds. So I would say screen is somewhat downgrade for me. Speaker sound is loud and clear and creates pleasant vibration in air. All I can say it has nice ring to it. With headphone (I use Samsung E5's headphone as there was no headphone in the Lenovo's package) it is noiseless hifi out put with support from Dolby Digital.
  
  Android Marshmallow 6.0 runs on K5.
  

  Pros:
  
  - 5.5 inches full hd lcd
  
  - 13mp rear cam with pdaf and 8mp front cam
  
  - sturdy metal frame
  
  -finger print scanner and it is fast.
  
  -exchange offer
  
  - Ant VR comes at just  500 with the mobile
  

  Cons:
  
  - heavy
  
  - comparitively thicker than my previous phone
  
  - lcd can not produce color as pleasant as Super Amoled
  
  -Xiomi offers better hardware at this price point.
  
  I am happy with this mobile and that's all matters.

column6: A Decent Phone for this Price Range
column7:
Hi All,
  

  Good day.
  

  I had received the device a day before and writing this review after a day usage.
  

  Pros:
  

  1. Display Clarity (Full HD and decent viewing angles)
  
  2. Speakers - With Dolby Atmos the speakers performs really well
  
  3. Touchscreen Response - Which is very fluid and highly sensitive ( It will not miss any simple touch)
  
  4. Performance - Smooth enough
  
  5. Design - Stylish with unibody metal casing (Especially Silver one IMO)
  
  6. Camera - Decent enough but not the best (Though front camera is performing to its level)
  
  7. Battery life - Good enough with 3500mAh battery. For Moderate to heavy users it will last for a day, else you can easily get 1.5 days. In my case with Wifi ON, around 2 hrs of calls and 3 hours of chatting, with in between internet and multimedia usage the battery reduced from 100% to 44% in 11 hours.
  
  8. Fingerprint Sensor - Unlocking time is quite ok, but not very fast.
  
  9. Signal Strength and call Quality - Awesome.
  
  10. RAM - 4GB is excellent, it will run huge number of apps in background without any lag.
  


  Cons:
  

  1. Slippery though it has a metal finishing it may slip from your hand any time. Better use with the cover.
  
  2. Though fingerprint sensor works fine, it is failing to recognize one or the other time.
  
  3. Hybrid slot - definitely a disappointment
  
  4. Single LED flash
  
  5. Feels bit bulky and heavy.
  
  6. Software - with series of bloatware of which most cant be uninstalled.
  


  As per my view, if you are camera lover and looking for more storage then you should have a look around. But if you need a decent enough performance with overall satisfaction then this one won't disappoint you definitely. And for this price range of 13499 you can definitely give this device a try without any regret.

Unbeatable VFM!
  

  Spent a hell lot of time deciding between this and the Redmi Note 3. No regrets at all till date.
  

  This is an amazing smartphone you can get for the money. Premium feel. Neither too heavy nor too thick. Loved the design. Bought the grey version so no ugly black borders around here.
  

  Slick and simple UI which's very close to stock android. Gotta do a 300MB update and see how things change. I hope this phone gets official Cyanogenmod support. Any devs reading? Please do!
  

  Good rear camera. Great front camera. The front camera pictures are great but the videos look slightly blurry at times and I hope Lenovo fixes it with a software update. Footages from the rear camera are good but Lenovo has to optimize the focusing algorithms with a software update. Low light performance is average but you can't ask for more for this price.
  

  The display is laminated but it doesn't have the wow factor certain laminated displays have. The icons don't pop out of the screen as much as you'd see on an iPhone 6S :P. Don't get me wrong. The display is very good and pleasant to look. The colours are great and everything looks very crisp. The touchscreen is pretty slick and very responsive too.
  

  The fingerprint sensor works just fine but I wish it could be calibrated a bit more for greater accuracy but it's a software thing anyway.
  

  The audio from the rear firing speaker is pretty awesome. It's not tinny at all, has a good bass response and it's pretty loud too. The audio from the 3.5mm jack is just amazing. It's pretty flat but it's crystal clear and loud enough. You can hear each of the notes hover around your ears.
  

  No. Lag. Observed. At. All. This is perhaps the most important thing for me. The four gigs underneath does it's job just fine.
  

  Being a power user, I tweak around a lot and I'm pretty confident that this phone can get through anything you throw at it without breaking a sweat. I don't give a shit about hardcore gaming (which it does manage quite well to a certain extent) so I'm good to go with a Helio P10. This phone has pretty decent hardware. Let's hope Lenovo does the same job on the software.
  

  (Will update after the update. Pun intended. :P)
  

  Update: I've been using this for around a week now.
  

  The good things:
  

  The phone is pretty good. It's quite snappy. It doesn't hang much. Doesn't heat up very fast. Handles pretty much everything you throw at it. Apps and games work just fine. Audio quality is awesome both from the loudspeaker and the 3.5mm jack. Battery lasts a day with average use. Front camera is truly great for selfies! Rear camera performs well for outdoors photos.
  

  The bad things:
  

  It's cumbersome to get a good image from the rear camera. Outdoor shots are very good. Indoors, the focus fails sometimes for macro shots and the images lack sharpness and detail. But some other times, the images turn out to be just fine. Video is average outdoors and not very impressive indoors. Front video is average outdoors and very noisy indoors.
  

  The camera can perform way better if it gets some good software optimization. The 300MB update I received did nothing in my experience.
  

  Some apps like Google Camera are not listed in the PlayStore. I tried installing it manually but it crashes the moment I run it. Come on Lenovo! We need good software!

column3: Lenovo K6 Power (Grey / Dark Grey, 32 GB)
column7:
This phone is truly amazing at this price, but there are a few shortcomings. I've ordered it recently and it arrived as expected. I purchased the 4GB Dark Gray version at 10,999.
  

  PROS:
  
  - Great look and feel. It looks beautiful while feeling quite heavy in your palm. The metallic body is very charming.
  
  - Just a few 10k phones support lightning fast fingerprint unlock and latest Android 6.0 perks.
  
  - Incredible sound. Powered by Dolby Atmos, the phone speakers actually burst out more decibels than my laptop (which is a Lenovo with Dolby as well).
  
  - 4GB RAM is more than enough. Although only half of it will be available in most general situations, 2GB is still pretty solid.
  
  - (Contd.) Switching b/w apps, playing games, and interacting with the phone in general, is very quick.
  
  - The battery is a mammoth. Once charged, you can keep using the phone for 2-3 days, all while playing games, 24*7 WiFi, watching videos, and listening to music every once a while.
  

  CONS:
  
  - Grip: The phone's grip is not safe. It's got a metal body but with the same curves as a normal phone. In fact, I dropped the phone after a few hours of buying, right on my marble floor (nothing happened btw). It should've had a more edgy grip to support the metal body.
  
  - Heating: The phone, being metal, heats on the back cover very fast. Similarly, it gets cold very fast if you keep it away for a while, even if on your bed. Metal is more sensitive to temperature changes.
  
  - Space: 8GB is taken up by the OS (Android 6.0). It happens in all phones, so that's nothing too unique. You're only left with 24GB of space for your stuff.
  
  - Camera: Camera, let me say, is DECENT. It's not really a con in itself. But when compared to other phones of the 10k range, surely the K6 Power has lesser to offer. Nevertheless, the images are crisp and it's got pretty okay low-light photography power.
  
  - Lack of quick charge mode might also bug certain people.
  
  - The earphones with the phone are a pain.

Lenovo K6 power
  
  I'm writing this review after 10 days of usage. Firstly, I got it at 10 K as offer price. It took 3 days to deliver the product.
  
  The mobile is awesome with the design and performance.
  
  Pro's:
  
  4gb RAM & 32gb ROM : you'll have 2gb & 23gb remaining memory
  
  Display: Full HD (doesn't support 4k videos) & IPS display
  
  Design: looks good but the panel is somewhat slippery
  
  OS: came with Android marshmallow & recently nougat also available for update
  
  Camera: 13mp rear professional like   with many features it's too good & 8 mp front camera, you can take very good quality selfei compare to others
  
  Battery: 4000mah non removable   can use for one day with all day browsing
  
  Sound: Dolby Atmos is awesome experience
  
  SIM: can use 2 nano Sims or one sim & memory card, supports Jio
  
  UI and apps: UI is quite good and no much pre installed apps
  
  Fingerprint: recognises in less than 1 sec, can add upto 5 finger prints
  
  No heating issues during working, but heat up's while charging becoz it has metal body.
  

  Con's:
  
  There are few things lacking
  
  Some times camera unable to save photo's don't know why.
  
  No separate music, video and gallery apps
  
  Slow charging, it takes almost 2 hours to full charge
  
  Placement of speaker's is not good, I could be in front either, so that we can experience some more better Dolby Atmos sound as in like lenovo k4 note
  
  It could have better microphone and earpiece
  

  So overall felt good phone @ 10K.
  
  If you feel the review is good please like & share.

column7:
Writing this up after using the mobile for 4 days.
  

  First of all, my microphone works good. No issues with it like many are facing...
  

  Here are the pros and cons :-->
  

  Pros :
  

  1) Good Battery Backup
  
  2) Sound quality
  
  3)Never Hangs
  
  4)Dolby Atmos Rocks
  
  5) HD Display
  
  6) Performance
  


  Cons:
  

  1) Camera Quality. Decent, but could have been better.
  
  2) Sound is muted when the device is placed facing up. An elevation near the speaker would have made it better.

Ok, so usually I don't review products. But, as it can be seen that this review section is cancerous. I would like to review my Lenovo K6 Power(4GB RAM).
  
  P.S. - I am going to cover only exceptions (good and bad). Rest you can expect reasonable and as expected.
  

  PROS -
  

  RAM Management - You will always have 2-3 gb of ram at your disposal, no matter how much multitasking is done.
  

  Battery Life - I received my fone at 76% battery. Used it for continuous 5-6 hrs. Kept my fone down at 36% at night. In morning it was showing 34%. Enough said !
  

  Dolby Atmos - In love with it's sound quality. Best exp i have had in sound dept. ( I was once an owner of Sony Xperia Z1).
  

  Display - Full HD Display. Sharp and crisp.
  

  Stylish Look and design.
  

  Just to remind you guys, that this fone just costs 11k. ( I got mine in 9k).
  

  CONS -
  

  A Little buggy UI - It hasn't got the smoothest  of UI. Sometimes it lacks in smooth transition.
  

  Built Quality - Its decent. Not too impressed by it.
  

  Again, costs just 11k.
  

  Now, so many people complaining about headset. Consider it a gift from Lenovo. Other fones  at this budget don't give one. Use a good earphone and exp DOLBY ATMOS sound quality.
  

  All in all a keeper. Totally a worth for money.
  
  Exceeded my expectations for a low budget fone.
  
  This was my honest review. Hope you guys will find it useful !

column3: Lenovo K6 Power (Grey / Dark Grey, 32 GB)
column7:
This phone is amazing at this price, but there are a few shortcomings. I've ordered it recently and it arrived as expected. I purchased the 4GB Dark Gray version at 10,999.
  

  PROS:
  
  - Great look and feel. It looks beautiful while feeling quite heavy in your palm. The metallic body is very charming.
  
  - Just a few 10k phones support lightning fast fingerprint unlock and latest Android 6.0.
  
  - Incredible sound. Powered by Dolby Atmos.
  
  - 4GB RAM is more than enough. Although only half of it will be available in most general situations, 2GB is still pretty solid.
  
  - (Contd.) Switching b/w apps, playing games, and interacting with the phone in general, is very quick.
  
  - The battery is a mammoth. Once charged, you can keep using the phone for 2-3 days, all while playing games, 24*7 WiFi, watching videos, and listening to music every once a while.
  

  CONS:
  
  - Grip: The phone's grip is not safe. It's got a metal body but with the same curves as a normal phone. In fact, I dropped the phone after a few hours of buying.
  
  - Heating: The phone, being metal, heats on the back cover very fast. Similarly, it gets cold very fast if you keep it away for a while, even if on your bed. Metal is more sensitive to temperature changes.
  
  - Camera: Camera, let me say, is DECENT. It's not really a con in itself. But when compared to other phones of the 10k range, surely the K6 Power has lesser to offer. Nevertheless, the images are crisp and it's got pretty okay low-light photography power.
  
  - Lack of quick charge mode might also bug certain people.
  
  - The earphones with the phone are a pain.

column3: Lenovo K6 Power (Grey / Dark Grey, 32 GB)
column7:
Good budget phone with few cons :-
  
  I bought 4 gb variant of this phone and was pretty impressed by its performance and battery backup. But there are quite a few cons too with it.
  

  Pros:
  
  1. Budget priced smartphone with really good overall performance
  
  2. 4gb memory ( out of which 2+ gb is free all the time)
  
  3. Amazing battery backup of at least 2 days (an hour of gaming, half hour of calls, wifi on 24 hours)
  
  3. Good gaming performance
  
  4. Loud dual speakers
  
  3. Dolby Atmos sounds great with good quality earphones.
  
  4. Mind blowing VR experience with dedicated VR mode ( used AntVR glasses abd you can experience everything  in VR mode, experience it to believe it  )
  
  5. Good for one hand use, as I was tired of using 5.5 inch phones that look good for flaunting but are unusable with one hand and your thumb starts paining. But this size solved the issue, not so big and not so small.
  
  6. Good screen clarity, excellent resolution and brightness
  
  7. Camera is better than equivalent phones in its range in sunlight and well lit indoor conditions but struggles in dark surroundings.
  
  8. Good call reception.
  
  9. Inbuilt call recording feature
  
  10. Double tap to wake up the screen
  
  11. Easy screenshot feature
  
  12. Lenovo brand value and service centre availability is much better than any Chinese brand. So you can rest peacefully
  


  Cons:-
  
  1. When you pick it up for the first time you will notice that its a bit heavier for its size but manageable
  
  2. BIG PROBLEM - if you set your favorite ringtone, sometimestime it will not ring and  you'll miss your calls and alarms.
  
  3. Sometimes I feel the fingerprint sensor is just for show, it gets set easily but there is a compulsion of setting a number pin for backup. And when you try to unlock your phone by touching the same finger it will still ask you to enter the number pin ( happens most of the times, very rarely it will unlock only with finger print) it is very irritating to use the fingerprint and number pin both most of the times. And you will feel embarrassed if someone asks you to show fingerprint feature and will make fun of you saying whats the use of fingerprint when you have to enter pin also)
  
  4. Heats a lot while charging and a little bit while gaming.
  
  5. Whatever setting you do do for app installation, apps will still get installed in  phone memory, so better get a 32+ gb memory card but its only possible if you use only one sim
  
  6. Sometimes wifi connectivity is poor
  
  7. The headphone jack is on the top, it will confuse you until you get habitual.
  
  8. There is a feature which allows you to hold the phone directly on your  ear to answer a call. I thought it would be convenient but it answers call when pick up the phone  in your hand and just when you are thinking to answer or not the other  person says "Hello"
  
  9. Only 32 gb memory when the competitors are offering 64
  
  10. The notifications pop up only when you unlock the phone, which means you will get the notifications and messages very late unless you keep unlocking your phone just to check. But it is a Marshmallow's bug
  
  10. No OTA updates to update to Android -7 Nougat
  

  So overall it is a balance of good and bad, you will be happy with its battery and performance and sometimes you will also curse it for its cons. But I would say you can still live with it.

  Although my redmi note 3 still uses 3gb ram what I have found is the ram left after using the same number of apps on both, the phab 2 still has approx 1.72gb of ram free whereas the Redmi note 3 has only 1.2 to 1.5gb free which is a remarkable spec considering the display size is massively huge in Lenovo Phab 2.
  
  Theres no lag in the apps and the the smartphone works butter smooth.theres no heating issue at all even with the phone being on charge for a long time. The redmi note 3 has ample amount of heating issue. The ram the storage is more than enough and u can slide a massive 128gb micro sd card to expand beyond the normal level.

  Guys remember this is a sub 10k range phone so dont expect this to have a brilliant display like samsung or infinity display type stuff. Saying that I just loved this display at 65-70% brightness and a great Airtel 4g connection, HD videos on youtube are a treat to watch. the display is crisp, colors ae good and the screen melts into the bezel so effeortlessly that you wont need a tv or a larger monitor once u a re habituated with this device.   with so many thing s in mind went for the OTA update and trust me the phone seems superbbb 4g aiirtel is running like a mad speed and its  awesomely col while charged up and low battery issues solved.

  I am an avid MI user and practically I feel no phone can match to the hardware and software tuning that an MI device gives. bee using a MI note, note 3, note 4 and also possess an MI Max9the big daddy).
  

  this is an honest review after 3 weeks of intense usage.
  
  I will go straight to the specs.
  
  Dont think anything about the processing power, its mindblowing .A massive 3 GB RAM, MediaTek (MTK 8735) quad-core processor, the Lenovo Phab 2 takes your smartphone experience to the next level for sure.
  
  Although my redmi note 3 still uses 3gb ram what I have found is the ram left after using the same number of apps on both, the phab 2 still has approx 1.72gb of ram free whereas the Redmi note 3 has only 1.2 to 1.5gb free which is a remarkable spec considering the display size is massively huge in Lenovo Phab 2.
  
  Theres no lag in the apps and the the smartphone works butter smooth.theres no heating issue at all even with the phone being on charge for a long time. The redmi note 3 has ample amount of heating issue. The ram the storage is more than enough and u can slide a massive 128gb micro sd card to expand beyond the normal level.
  
  Now comes the most important part the display.
  

  Guys remember this is a sub 10k range phone so dont expect this to have a brilliant display like samsung or infinity display type stuff. Saying that I just loved this display at 65-70% brightness and a great Airtel 4g connection, HD videos on youtube are a treat to watch. the display is crisp, colors ae good and the screen melts into the bezel so effeortlessly that you wont need a tv or a larger monitor once u a re habituated with this device. Chats and scrolling fb , twitter are so easy with the big display. Also needs to be mentioned is the touch responsiveness which is simply awesome, the touch reponse is so good u can actually somehow use the device with one hand although its big for one hand usage.
  
  I guess the back side is removable which is a great thing  considering the massive battery and the heat dissipitation once can expect from a device.
  
  Only one small issue I felt was the lack of enough battery for a heavy usage user like me for the entire day but who cares till you have a MI or ROMOSS power bank with you. the battery lasts for one complete day with oderate to heavy usage and remember by usage i am meaning Airtel 4g usage. streaming, whatsapp, fb continously with almost 2hrs of talktime daily and 2 hrs of music almost thats a great battery but if it would have been 5000mah it was awesome. 4050mah is descent and does justice.
  
  theres no fingerprint scanner but doenst matter much as this is a budget phablet.
  
  The smartphone is 4g enabled and it always receive 4g for sure. the secondary sim is a 2g one.
  

  theres no call block facility in lenovo so I have installed the Zen Asus UI dialer for the same, now its a complete mean machine.
  

  Laslty the Dolby ATMOS my goodness the sound effect surpasses the reproduction quality of my 5000rs pioneer car stereo impact. Audio quality is a tricky stuff as i am weariing a spec so cannot put the phone so big on the ears but with earphones the audio s awesome voice call clarity is simply superb.

I bought this product very recently (it has not been a month yet). I got it in pristine condition and it works just great. Gaming, reading using apps all are good but since last couple of days it is showing some problems with the battery and the mic. The problem at first was that the  phab immediately after showing 24% charge (within seconds, not minutes) it turned on battery saver and showed that the charge left was 15% and just after that it shut down. And the other problem is that sometimes when taking a call I can hear the caller but the person on the other end seems to be not receiving any audio from my end. The problem with the mic is solved by rebooting but this one occurs more often than the other one. By the way before anything else I must say that all the apps running are from google play store only and most of them are supported by google. This phone is really good in terms of working, reading, browsing and even gaming. If these issue had not come up I would not have written this review instead just would have given the product 4 stars this much good of a product this is in terms of performance.

column6: ONE OF THE BEST QUAD HD PHONES AT THIS PRICE
column7:
I was about to purchase an LG G3 or a nexus 6 when I glanced upon this phone.  I searched the internet for reviews but could only find a few of them, all of them complained about one issue - heating of the phone.
  

  I received this phone in record time from Flipkart under their offer of Rs.29,999.  The Phone's quality is excellent.
  

  Some of the best features of the phone are:
  

  1. Great Screen - Clear and crisp and very high quality though some reviews talked about saturation etc.  To me it is a fantastic screen.
  
  2. Great Size - I was very hesitant to buy this due to the size of the screen at six inches.  However Lenovo has done a great job is making the size manageable.  It is nice to hold in the hand and does not feel odd.  The thin bezels make this almost the same size as the Note 4 and the Iphone 6 plus and marginally smaller than the nexus 6.
  
  3. Camera - Fantastic one and it takes great pictures.  The camera however protrudes outside the phone, it would have been great if Lenovo did not reduce the thickness of the phone so much.  The other option for them would have been to include a piece of metal for the full width of the phone (currently the black band behind) which is thick to cover this protrusion.
  
  4. Metal back - Good quality aluminium finish makes the phone look premium.  I only hope that Lenovo and Flipkart make available all the colours (I personally liked the silver more than the black which I got).
  
  5. Battery - The battery at 4000 mah lasts a full day with occasional video and use of pictures.  Considering the screen size and resolution this is as best as it can get at this time.
  
  6. Processor - It has a very good snapdragon processor which is the same as the LG G3 though one notch below the Note 4 and the Nexus 6.  There is no lag in performance as stated in some reviews.
  

  Please download the software update before you start using the phone.  This eliminates the heating problem which I never encountered.
  

  Lenovo also sent a screen guard along with this, a nice gesture.  Would have appreciated if they had included the flip cover even at a marginal extra cost.
  

  The only drawback I can say (adding this just because I have to) is there is no timeline on the lollipop update and the protruding camera (which i worry I may damage if I put the phone in a pouch or a case).  The phone's memory at 32GB is enough for me though this may be insufficient for some.
  

  To end, if you are looking to buy a Quad HD Phone (Phablet) this is the best buy at this price.
  

  Note : I hope flipkart and their suppliers start selling more accessories for this phone like a metal bumper etc. quickly.

This is one Smartphone that is a real "VFM - Value for Money" High End Android 4.4 Smartphone with the following features -
  

  8mm Thick, 180 gm weight,
  
  3 GB RAM, 32 GB Internal Memory,
  
  6 inch Corning Gorilla Glass 3 Screen, QHD Display,
  
  4000 mAH Battery Dual Sim Phone,
  
  16 MP Auto-focus high end professional back camera with flash and 5MP Front Camera,
  
  Secure Zone and Open Zone segregation for Apps (Official & Personal Data containerization respectively),
  
  All Metal Body,
  
  NFC, VPN,
  
  Can be switched between Stock Android UI and Lenovo UI seamlessly
  
  IP Phone configurable features etc.
  

  The Phone also has CloneIT App to allow for seamless Data transfer of Contacts, SMSs, Photos, Files, Apps in your old smartphone to this new one through Bluetooth. I have used this effectively to move all my Data from the Galaxy Grand Duos.
  

  I also ordered for a Lenovo original Vibe Pro Z2 Cover from the Foison Group (costing USD 16.67 incld Singapore Post postage fees) on www.aliexpress.com and I received the Flip Cover in an Excellent condition in less than 2 weeks. Once I put my Lenovo Vibe Pro Z2 into the cover, the phone really turned a Beauty. You must experience it with the original flip cover!!!
  

  I have also purchased a Micro USB to USB OTG Cable separately as I plan to store or shift Data in the Vibe Pro Z2 Smartphone onto my 2 TB External HDD.

column3: Lenovo Vibe Z2 Pro (Starry Night Black, 32 GB)
column6: Note 4, LG G3, One Plus One, iPhone 6+, Mi4....You Are Served.
column7:
This is updated review after using the phone for 2 weeks.
  
  +Pros:
  
  1. Performance: This mobile is an absolute beast. Scoring 42,000 in Antutu, that's like 50% more than Nexus 5. Throw anything at it and it won't break any sweat.
  
  2. Display: Everyone's reaction to the display is WHOOAA. This device sets the new benchmark with its 6 inch display. Best thing is it's not bigger than note3/4. That's some serious engineering by Lenovo. Even iPhone 6 plus (with 5.5'' display) is bigger than this mobile. By nits measurements the display is almost twice as much bright as LG G3 and Note 4. No complain for color reproduction or viewing angles either.
  
  3.. Battery life: With moderate use battery easily lasts 2 days . All Lenovo phones have battery saving algorithms. Although the battery life is not as legendary as Lenovo P780 but it still is a lot more than others. The mobile can last for a week without charging in emergency power mode(only calling and messaging). LG G3 which is fatter, has smaller display and only half as much bright has only 4-5 hours of screen time whereas this mobile has 9-10 hours of screen time.
  
  4. Camera: Hats off to both cameras, low lighting photography is absolutely brilliant. With manual mode you get so much control you can actually capture stars at night.  Same for videos also. 4K videos have more details than FHD Blu Ray. In low lighting conditions, video is automatically switched to 15FPS to preserve the details. The camera (lens and sensor) is same from twice priced Note4. Slow motion capturing is also present but up to 120FPS only. Front facing camera is also good. I'll say it's better than my 4 year old Rs. 15k Sony 14MP P&S camera. No kidding.
  
  5. OS: It has the features of MIUI as Xiaomi compiles OS for Lenovo. App drawer is not missed. This OS is more customizable than stock Android. Shortcuts are everywhere. For most of the tasks you'll need 2-3 fewer clicks than stock android saving you some time. Yes, it has few bugs but Lenovo is always fixing. I've received 2 updates so far. I'd like to mention 2 plus points for the OS.
  
  Secure Zone -> This is more like second OS running parallel. And no, it doesn't strain hardware for that. It's marvelous. It has its own settings like wallpapers etc. You can have two instances of same application(say whatsapp, skype) running in normal zone and in secure zone(no need to install it twice). I absolutely love this functionality. I run two instances of whatsapp for personal  and business use.
  
  Stock Android -> Those who are fans of vanilla android they will like this. Boot in nexus like stockness.
  
  6. Double Sim: Crucial functionality for any professional, businessman or frequent traveler. This feature alone kills the competition.
  
  7. App firewall: You can revoke certain app's permissions through this. For example it won't let a single application to read your contacts unless you allow it. Also antivirus/malware/spam protection comes inbuilt in the OS.
  
  8. Looks: This is one of the best looking phone out there. Period. Genuine design, thin bezels around display, and slim profile makes this mobile very professional looking.
  

  -Cons:
  
  1. I think QHD is just a marketing gimmick. I have worked in graphics industry and I don't think I'll notice any difference between QHD and FHD at such small display size. QHD with its almost twice pixel count (3.7MP) compared to FHD (2MP) only is a deadweight on the processor.
  
  2. Screen Density (different from pixel density) is low. Meaning everything looks very big. 5x6 icon layout should have been provided instead 4x5. Text is big. etc. Lenovo has wasted real estate of 6 inch display. It's not like competition is doing anything different. One can fix this by rooting the phone.
  

  =Other Thoughts:
  
  1. Device does heat up when doing heavy gaming or when using camera. Actually that's quite expected of power hungry snapdragon 800/1/5 processors. On this device it's more noticeable because of its slim profile, everything inside is dense and secondly it has metal back.
  
  2. Speaker is very loud. Provided headphones are rather average sound quality with smaller tips. Bigger tips are not provided.
  
  3. It supports for wireless display. Miracast and All-share supported. DLNA isn't.
  
  4. 5Ghz AC Wifi support is there.
  
  5. Flash is in two stage, First for just torch, second which is 10x brighter  is for photography.
  
  6. FM recording is inbuilt in the radio app.
  
  7. Most of the third party bloatware can be removed.
  
  8. Notification LED is there but limited notification are offered.
  
  9. Battery drain is 1% to every 2 mins use of camera.  Single minute of 4K video takes about 600mb space.
  
  10. Inbuilt Lithium Polymer battery is better than Lithium Ion in many aspects such as shelf life, total charging cycles, no heating problem.
  
  11. Lenovo has forgotten to give settings to change the resolution for taking photos. 16MP is default. You can use third party app to capture low res photos.
  

  If you like my review, hit yes.

column3: Lenovo Vibe Z2 Pro (Starry Night Black, 32 GB)
column6: (Updated review) - A high spec'd phone that DOESN'T perform to its potential ! Dual SIM is a nice bonus.
column7:
(Scroll down to see my update to this review.)
  
  I ordered this phone on Sun, 19-Oct.  I was promised a delivery of 28-Oct (given the holiday rush).  However, the order delivered at Chennai by Tuesday (21-Oct) afternoon itself !  This was the 3rd item I had ordered from Flipkart, and each time, they have exceeded expectations in delivery.
  

  Now for the Vibe Z2 Pro.
  

  I have a OnePlus One (64GB) and an HTC One M8.  The OnePlus One is superb while the One M8 is ok, not as smooth and battery was no where close to OnePlus One's.  Since I wanted an high end dual sim phone, I went for the HTC One E8 Dual (which was the only available phone with high end specs + dual sim), which I bought for around ?34k.  Even though it had the same high end specs as the M8, it does not perform as well.  It stutters a LOT even for basic operations (opening/closing dialer, opening/closing camera, switching apps, etc).
  
  So I was back in the market searching for a dual sim high end phone when I came across the Lenovo Vibe Z2 Pro (I just wish they had a shorter, more impactful name!).  I read ALL the reviews on Flipkart as of 19-Oct when I placed the order (and even after I placed the order) and also whatever video reviews were available in English on YouTube (which aren't many though).
  

  I've now used the phone for the last 4 days, and I'm happy to report that the phone is a BEAST.  The screen, the brightness levels, battery and the performance is really top notch.  Though the volume levels are high, the sound quality is ok, not great, but definitely passable.  As for gaming, I played Vector and ShadowFight 2 a lot, and there wasn't a single frame drop any time.
  

  I read a few people complaining about 'overheating'.  I played ShadowFight 2 for an hour continuously, and the phone slightly warmed up (remember, this has an all metal body).  I did NOT notice it heating up any other time (even when I used the camera for 10 minutes or so continuously).
  

  I love the way Lenovo was able to cram in a gorgeous 6 inch QHD display into such a compact form factor.  Lenovo's UI is neat & feature rich and neither heavy (like Samsung's) nor gimmicky.
  

  The battery life is more than acceptable.  For a 4000mah battery, one may expect more, but even with my medium-heavy usage, I easily get more than a day of battery life (though I charge all my phones & iPad through the night).
  

  32GB of internal memory (with about 23GB of memory available to the user) is more than enough for 99% of the users.  USB OTG support is useful if you need to store or transfer really large files.
  

  And finally, the price is good.  If this phone had been 4-5k more, I probably would have stayed away.
  

  Since the phone is made of metal, it is a little slippery.
  

  So far, I'm happy I purchased this phone.  I do hope it continues to perform the way it does for a long time.  A pat-on-the-back to Lenovo for this nice product (but like I mentioned, the marketing seems to be non-existent!).
  

  -------------------------------------
  
  Update - 25-Nov-14
  
  After using the phone for a little over a month, I have reduced my rating from 5 to 3 stars. Here's why:
  

  1) I was totally surprised to find that the OTA Firmware updates will NOT install if the phone is encrypted.  After a lot of chasing (the Lenovo call centre "technical team" did not even understand the word "encryption" for the first 5 mins!), this was confirmed to me by the Lenovo service centre at Chennai.  So each time you get a firmware update, the phone has to be factory reset !!  Absolutely idiotic.
  

  2) RAM usage is constantly high.  Even though the phone comes with 3GB of RAM, it always seems to utilize 2.2 to 2.5GB of RAM, and starts stuttering when more than 6-7 (regular) apps are open in the background.  You can install 'Clean Master' app to monitor your RAM usage on a real time basis using their widget.
  

  3) Battery life is average - Even though it comes with a massive, industry-leading 4000mah battery on paper, it does not seem to optimize operations which results in a below par battery life.  For light-medium users, you may easily get 1 full day out of it. It should perform much better than that but it doesn't !
  

  4) Default launcher unstable - under heavy usage, the launcher stops working and the phone has to be restarted. With the specs this phone comes with, its easily supposed to handle heavy usage.
  

  5) Heating - Though not that big an issue, but when I used Google Hangouts for more than 25 mins, the phone became dangerously hot. I had to re-boot the phone to cool it down.  Having a metal body, one can feel the heat easily. The advantage also is that it cools down fast as well.
  

  Overall, the performance of the phone with these specs is below par.  Lenovo now owns Motorola, and I expected much much more from this phone. Disappointed !
  

  27-Nov-14 - After switching back to Google UI (thank God Lenovo provided this option), the phone is a lot more stable and performs well. So, make it 3.5 on 5.
